zh: 11. 从黑格尔到马克思
en: 11. From Hegel to Marx

zh: 黑格尔主义的死胡同
en: HEGELIANISM AT A DEAD END

zh: 到了黑格尔这里，作为一种思想体系的哲学史达到了顶峰。在这个体系中，各个分支的发展是如此完备和全面，以至于人们感觉该说的话都已经说尽了。剩下的只是围绕同一主题进行无穷无尽的变奏，就像J. S. 巴赫那错综复杂的音乐世界一样。
en: With Hegel, we reach the pinnacle of the history of philosophy as a system of ideas. Here, the development of each branch of the system is so complete and comprehensive, that one feels that all that has to be said has already been said. All that is left is to spin an infinite number of variations on the same themes, as in the intricate sound-world of J. S. Bach.

zh: 然而，就在其取得最大胜利的时刻，黑格尔体系却开始走向不可逆转的衰落与瓦解。黑格尔主义的危机可以简单地解释：黑格尔将他包罗万象的体系推向了极致，以至于真正耗尽了哲学本身的所有可能性。他所提出的问题无法在纯粹观念体系的范围内得到解决。黑格尔方法的内在弱点在于：作为一位唯心主义者，他并非从真实、具体、感性的人类思想出发，而是从一种他称为“自我意识”的唯心主义抽象概念出发。在《精神现象学》中，黑格尔从意识的初级、胚胎阶段出发，经历了一系列阶段，这些阶段在总体上涵盖了人类思想的整个历史，从宗教，到哲学史，再到科学。
en: But, at the moment of its greatest triumph, the Hegelian system began to enter into irreversible decline and dissolution. The crisis of Hegelianism can be simply explained. Hegel carried his all-embracing system so far that it really exhausted the possibilities of philosophy as such. The problems he raised could not be resolved within the limits of a purely ideal system. The inherent weakness of Hegel’s method was that, as an idealist, he did not set out from real, concrete, sensuous human thought, but from an idealist abstraction, which he called self-consciousness. In his Phenomenology of Spirit, Hegel sets out from an elementary, embryonic stage of consciousness, proceeding through a whole series of stages, which in their totality embrace the entire history of human thought, from religion, through the history of philosophy, to science.

zh: 黑格尔的辩证法相较于先前的哲学是一个巨大的进步，其中包含许多深刻的洞见和天才的灵光。在某些地方（尤其是《历史哲学》中），他几乎接近唯物主义。但由于他的出发点是唯心主义，现实世界在这里只能以间接且扭曲的方式得到体现。正因如此，尽管黑格尔哲学无疑具有深邃的内涵和诸多精辟见解，黑格尔哲学最终仍陷入了僵局。
en: Hegel’s dialectical method was a huge advance over the earlier philosophy, and it contained many profound insights and flashes of genius. In places (notably, in The Philosophy of History) he comes close to materialism. But, since his starting point was idealism, the real world is here expressed only in an indirect and distorted manner. For this reason, in the end, despite all its undoubted profundity and its many brilliant insights, Hegelian philosophy found itself at an impasse.

zh: 《逻辑学》的出发点和顶点是“绝对理念”。这里的问题在于，黑格尔将主体与客体之间的关系彻底颠倒了。他的方法在某种意义上是客观的，因为它清晰地确立了现实事物和过程与其在意识中的反映之间的关系。然而，在黑格尔的理论中，思想与自身相异化，进入物质世界并在其中发展和展开，最终在漫长的演化之后回归自身，成为“绝对理念”——一种已吸纳了所有特殊性丰富内涵的普遍性。
en: The starting point and culmination of the Science of Logic was the Absolute Idea. The problem here was that Hegel stood the relation between subject and object on its head. His method is objective in the sense that it clearly establishes the relation between real things and processes, and their reflection in consciousness. However, in Hegel, thought alienates itself from itself, enters the material world and develops and unfolds within it, only to return to itself at the end of a lengthy evolution, as the Absolute Idea – a universal that has been enriched with all the wealth of the particular.

zh: “绝对理念”是已意识到自身的思想。但实际上，情况恰恰相反。在这里，现实仅仅是异化的思想，而现实状况却恰恰相反。说实话，整个理论体系不过是现实的幽灵般的回声。思想是已意识到自身的物质。我们不仅用头脑思考，还用所有的感官——事实上是用整个身体来思考。将人类与外部世界（自然）联系起来的，不是个体的抽象思维，而是人类集体的感性活动——社会劳动，它既改造自然，同时也改造人类自身。
en: The Absolute Idea is thought that has become conscious of itself. But, in reality, it is precisely the other way around. Here, reality is only alienated thought, whereas the exact opposite is the real state of affairs. To tell the truth, the entire edifice was merely a ghostly echo of reality. Thought is matter that has become conscious of itself. We do not think only with our mind but with all our senses – with our whole body in fact. What links humans with the external world (nature) is not the abstract thinking of individuals but collective human sensuous activity – social labour, which transforms nature, and at the same time transforms humankind itself.

zh: 黑格尔之后的黑格尔主义
en: HEGELIANISM AFTER HEGEL

zh: 一些哲学家试图按照黑格尔自己的思路，即在传统哲学的框架内，延续黑格尔未竟的事业。黑格尔主义右派的主要代表人物包括卡尔·弗里德里希·格歇尔、约翰·菲利普·加布勒、约翰·卡尔·弗里德里希·罗森克朗茨和约翰·爱德华·埃尔德曼等人。他们立足于黑格尔思想中最薄弱、最保守的一面。
en: Some philosophers tried to continue where Hegel had left off in his own terms, i.e. within the framework of traditional philosophy. The Hegelian Right were represented by men like Karl Friedrich Göschel, Johann Philipp Gabler, Johann Karl Friedrich Rosenkranz and Johann Eduard Erdmann. They based themselves on the weakest, most conservative side of Hegel.

zh: 在他们看来，黑格尔的辩证法已经发展到了极致，所需要的只是机械地重复陈词滥调，这些陈词滥调可以以一种外在的方式应用于任何内容。这比其他任何因素都更导致了辩证法的声名狼藉，许多人开始将其视为一种纯粹的言辞诡辩和狡辩。这些自诩为黑格尔门徒的人，既继承了恩师的所有缺点，却毫无其美德。他们的尝试显然未能产生任何有价值的东西，其水平远逊于这位伟人的著作。如今，他们已不再是历史的脚注。他们的著作毫无可取之处，其名字也早已被理所当然地遗忘。
en: For them, the Hegelian dialectic had been carried to its completion, and all that was required was the mechanical repetition of old phrases, which could be applied in an external manner to any content. This, more than anything, resulted in the discrediting of dialectics, which many began to see as a mere exercise in verbal tricks and sophistry. These self-proclaimed disciples of Hegel possessed all of the master’s defects and none of his virtues. Their attempts signally failed to produce anything of interest, and are far inferior to the writings of the great man. They are now no longer a footnote to history. Their writings contain nothing of note and their names have long been consigned to a well-earned oblivion.

zh: 黑格尔主义作为反动工具
en: HEGELIANISM AS A TOOL OF REACTION

zh: 对于右派黑格尔主义者而言，专制的普鲁士国家代表了社会发展的最高点。在这方面，他们似乎正追随其导师的脚步。但实际上，这仅仅代表了黑格尔思想的一面——最薄弱、也最无趣的一面。黑格尔的哲学观点无疑既带有神秘主义色彩，又具有唯心主义倾向；他在政治立场上（至少在晚年）持保守立场，倾向于支持普鲁士专制国家。是的，这一切都是事实，也是众所周知的。但这并不能穷尽我们正在讨论的问题，也未能如实反映黑格尔思想中本质性的、辩证的性质。
en: For the Right Hegelians, the autocratic Prussian state represented the highest point of all social development. In this, they seemed to be following in the footsteps of their master. But in reality, this represents only one side of Hegel’s thought – the weakest and least interesting side. Hegel, whose philosophical views were undoubtedly both mystical and idealist, was (at least in his later years) conservative in his political views and tended to support the Prussian Absolutist state. Yes, all this is true and well known. But it does not exhaust the matter under discussion and does not do justice to the essential, dialectical nature of Hegel’s thinking.

zh: 事实上，德国当局很快就意识到了黑格尔辩证法所蕴含的颠覆性和革命性含义。德国哲学界意识到其构成的危险，竭力与黑格尔划清界限，转而支持“回归康德”运动。但在其他国家，黑格尔主义却因其保守的一面而受到热烈欢迎。英国的情况尤为如此，在那里，黑格尔思想中的神秘主义和唯心主义元素被视为对抗唯物主义的有效解药。
en: In fact, the German authorities were quick to grasp the subversive and revolutionary implications of Hegel’s dialectic. Realising the danger posed by it, the philosophical establishment in Germany made every effort to distance itself from Hegel, preferring to support the ‘Back to Kant’ movement. But in other countries, Hegelianism was eagerly welcomed for its conservative side. That was particularly the case in Britain, where the mystical, idealist elements of Hegel were seen as a useful antidote to materialism.

zh: 盎格鲁-撒克逊世界中的黑格尔主义
en: HEGELIANISM IN THE ANGLO-SAXON WORLD

zh: 此时，宗教正在面对科学的前进——尤其是查尔斯·达尔文的进化论思想——展开一场绝望的后卫战，这些思想对“创世”观念乃至至高无上的造物主上帝的存在构成了直接威胁。正是对唯物主义——及其所蕴含的颠覆性和革命性内涵——的恐惧，才解释了19 世纪最后几十年里黑格尔主义在英国大学中本难以解释的流行现象。
en: By this time, religion was fighting a desperate rearguard action against the advance of science, in particular the evolutionary ideas of Charles Darwin, which posed a direct threat to the idea of Creation, and even to the existence of God the Supreme Creator. It was precisely the fear of materialism – with its subversive and revolutionary connotations – that explains the otherwise inexplicable popularity of Hegelianism in British universities in the last decades of the nineteenth century.

zh: 英国学术界寻求一种哲学武器来击溃唯物主义这头怪兽，最终在黑格尔唯心主义中找到了它。正如约翰·帕斯莫尔所指出的：“在德国，黑格尔主义完全未能遏制唯物主义的进步；但事实是，它被引入英国正是为了实现这一目的。”
同样，在美国，圣路易斯黑格尔学派认为，他们在黑格尔的哲学中找到了“一把剑，用来击溃政治中的无政府主义、宗教中的传统主义以及科学中的自然主义这头三头怪兽”。
en: The British academic establishment searched for a philosophical weapon to strike down the monster of materialism, and found it in Hegelian idealism. As John Passmore points out: “In Germany, Hegelianism had completely failed to arrest the progress of materialism; the fact remains that it was introduced into Great Britain to fulfil that very purpose.”

Similarly, in the USA, the St. Louis Hegelians thought they had found in his philosophy “a sword wherewith to smite the three-headed monster of anarchy in politics, traditionalism in religion and naturalism in science”.

zh: 我们目睹了这样一幕令人惊叹的景象：德国哲学（或者更准确地说，是德国哲学的讽刺画）被引入英国大学，而“认识论”——这一英国经验主义的附庸——却被输出到德国，并在那里受到了同样热烈的欢迎。有一段时间，传统的角色发生了逆转，但无论哪一方，结果都并不理想。J. H. 斯特林的著作《黑格尔的秘密》（1865）便是英国庸俗化黑格尔主义的典型代表，有人对此评论道：“如果黑格尔有什么秘密，斯特林确实守得很好！”这位伟人尚在世时，却鲜少受到英国哲学界主流的关注。该界对经验主义的痴迷，滋生了对抽象思维和广泛理论概括的根深蒂固的不信任，这已成为迄今为止所有盎格鲁-撒克逊哲学的持久弱点。
en: We have the astonishing spectacle of German philosophy (or, more accurately, a caricature of German philosophy) being imported into British universities, while the ‘theory of knowledge’ – that handmaiden of English empiricism – was exported to Germany, where it was met with equal enthusiasm. For a time, the traditional roles were reversed, with not very positive results in either case. Typical of the British school of vulgarised Hegelianism was the work of J. H. Stirling, The Secret of Hegel (1865), of which some remarked that: “If Hegel had a secret, Stirling kept it well!” While the great man was still alive, he received scant attention from the British philosophical establishment, whose obsession with empiricism gave rise to a deep-seated mistrust of abstract thought and broad theoretical generalisations which has been the enduring weakness of all Anglo-Saxon philosophy up to the present day.

zh: 黑格尔学派的瓦解
en: THE DISSOLUTION OF THE HEGELIAN SCHOOL

zh: 在德国，黑格尔学派因内部腐朽而分裂为若干相互争斗的派别，情况则有所不同。1831 年黑格尔去世后，他的学派不可避免地解体并分崩离析，成为自身内部矛盾的牺牲品。黑格尔主义的衰落注定会引发反响，而事实也确实如此。黑格尔学派分裂为左右两派。其中一种表现形式就是马克思主义，它彻底脱离了哲学（至少是迄今为止所理解的哲学）。
en: In Germany, where the inner decay of the Hegelian School had led to its dissolution into a number of squabbling sects, the situation was different. After the death of Hegel in 1831, his School inevitably disintegrated and fell to pieces, a victim of its own internal contradictions. The decay of Hegelianism was bound to provoke a reaction, and it did. The Hegelian School split into two wings – the right and left. One expression of this was Marxism, which led away from philosophy altogether (at least, philosophy as hitherto understood).

zh: 正是马克思和恩格斯将黑格尔思想中健康的内核从被遗忘的境地中拯救出来，并将其恢复为辩证唯物主义和历史唯物主义。科学社会主义奠基人的早期著作清楚地展现了其黑格尔主义的渊源。与黑格尔的真正清算，可追溯至《神圣家族》、《德意志意识形态》，尤其是著名的《关于费尔巴哈的提纲》。但马克思主义并非像雅典娜从宙斯头中诞生那样，一蹴而就、全副武装。马克思和恩格斯首先必须经历黑格尔左派的预备学校。
en: It was Marx and Engels who rescued the healthy kernel of Hegel’s thought from oblivion and restored it as dialectical and historical materialism. The early writings of the founders of scientific socialism clearly display their Hegelian origins. The real settling of accounts with Hegel can be traced to The Holy Family, The German Ideology and, particularly, the famous ‘Theses on Feuerbach’. But Marxism did not spring, ready formed and armed, like Athena from the head of Zeus. Marx and Engels first had to pass through the preparatory school of the Hegelian Left.

zh: 黑格尔左派
en: THE HEGELIAN LEFT

zh: 正如我们所指出的，黑格尔右派中没有一位值得一提的人物。远比他们更有意思的是围绕一群激进的德国自由思想家而凝聚起来的左翼，该派系是为反对保守反动派而形成的。这些勇敢的年轻人被称为“青年黑格尔派”（Junghegelianer）、“左派黑格尔派”（Linkshegelianer）或“黑格尔左翼”（die Hegelsche Linke），他们试图从黑格尔的哲学中得出激进的结论。
en: As we have noted, the Hegelian Right produced not one figure worthy of mention. Far more interesting was the left wing that crystallised around a group of radical German freethinkers, formed in opposition to the conservative reactionaries. Known variously as the Young Hegelians (Junghegelianer), the Left Hegelians (Linkshegelianer), or the Hegelian Left (die Hegelsche Linke), these brave young men attempted to draw radical conclusions from Hegel’s philosophy.

zh: 这绝非偶然。“青年黑格尔派”是当时德国宗教、哲学和政治动荡的产物。这一时期介于1830 年法国革命（该革命推翻了反动的波旁王朝君主查理十世）与1848 年至1849 年席卷欧洲（包括德国）的革命浪潮之间。“黑格尔左派”代表了黑格尔追随者中的激进派。他们在19 世纪30 年代和40 年代十分活跃，本着德国自由主义的精神来诠释黑格尔的思想。其主要成员包括大卫·施特劳斯、阿诺德·鲁格、马克斯·施蒂纳以及布鲁诺·鲍尔和埃德加·鲍尔。但其中也包括路德维希·费尔巴哈和摩西·赫斯。年轻时的马克思和恩格斯起初也曾参与这一运动。
en: This was no accident. The Young Hegelians were the product of the religious, philosophical, and political ferment in Germany at that time. This was the period between the Revolution of 1830 in France, which overthrew the reactionary Bourbon monarch Charles X, and the wave of revolutions that swept Europe – including Germany – in 1848 and 1849. The Hegelian Left represented the radical wing of Hegel’s followers. Active in the 1830s and 1840s, they interpreted Hegel’s ideas in the spirit of German liberalism. Their leading members were David Strauss, Arnold Ruge, Max Stirner, and Bruno and Edgar Bauer. But they also included Ludwig Feuerbach and Moses Hess. The young Marx and Engels were also initially involved in this movement.

zh: 尽管该学派标榜革命，但其关注点完全集中在抽象的哲学问题和宗教批判上，这体现在大卫·施特劳斯1835年出版的《耶稣生平》（Das Leben Jesu）一书中。该书对《圣经》进行了批判性分析，将耶稣描绘成一位普通的历史人物。施特劳斯将此归因于神话观念的传统延续。后来，布鲁诺·鲍尔主张宗教是一种“虚假意识”，而耶稣这一人物则是虚构的。施特劳斯和布鲁诺·鲍尔对《新约》进行的激进批判，标志着圣经研究领域的重要进步。这为马克思和恩格斯关于宗教的著作奠定了基础，也为考茨基后来那部历史唯物主义的杰作《基督教的根基》铺平了道路。
en: Despite its revolutionary claims, this school was entirely preoccupied with abstract philosophical questions and the criticism of religion, reflected in the publication in 1835 of The Life of Jesus (Das Leben Jesu) by David Strauss. This was a critical analysis of the Bible, in which Jesus is portrayed as an ordinary historical personality. Strauss explained this by the traditional persistence of mythological ideas. Later, Bruno Bauer argued that religion was a false consciousness, and that the person of Jesus was a fiction. The radical critique of the New Testament carried out by Strauss and Bruno Bauer represented an important step forward in biblical studies. It laid the basis for the writings of Marx and Engels on religion, and later Kautsky’s masterly work of historical materialism, The Foundations of Christianity.

zh: 对于那个时代而言，这些理论非常大胆且先进。在普遍的反动思潮和令人窒息的审查制度背景下，挑战教会的观念需要极大的勇气。但尽管他们取得了一些进展，其总体方法论仍停留在唯心主义层面，因此注定无法产生实质性成果。一个主要关注点是：虚假意识如何在社会中产生，并成为支配人们思想的力量。青年黑格尔派讨论的抽象性，部分源于严格的审查制度。但艺术、文学和宗教是唯一允许存在一定程度批判性思考的领域。
en: These were very bold and advanced theories for those times. It took courage to challenge the ideas of the church in the context of general reaction and suffocating censorship. But although they made some advances, their general approach remained idealist, and therefore was condemned to sterility. One of the main concerns was the question of how false consciousness arises in society and becomes a power over the minds of men. The abstract nature of the Young Hegelians’ discussions was partly a result of the strict laws of censorship. But art, literature and religion were the only fields where some degree of critical thought were permitted.

zh: 大约在1840 年，随着弗里德里希·威廉四世登基导致新闻审查有所放松，青年黑格尔派内部开始出现政治争论。尽管如此，他们关于宗教、哲学和政治的论述仍被晦涩抽象的术语所掩盖，其特征是反复使用“批判”一词。这种风格后来在马克思和恩格斯的著作中，如《德意志意识形态》和《神圣家族》，遭到了讽刺。尽管措辞听起来颇具激进色彩，但两位主要的青年黑格尔派代表——施特劳斯和鲍尔——之间的辩论仍未超出黑格尔唯心主义体系的范畴。施特劳斯认为，福音书中的传说源于早期基督教群体的自发、潜意识的神话创造，是人民精神的体现。
en: In about 1840, political arguments emerged in the ranks of the Young Hegelians, when the enthronement of Friedrich Wilhelm IV led to a certain relaxation of press censorship. Nevertheless, their pronouncements on religion, philosophy and politics were veiled in an obscure and abstract terminology, characterised by the repeated use of the word ‘critique’. This was later satirised by the writings of Marx and Engels such as The German Ideology and The Holy Family. Despite its radical-sounding phraseology, the debate between the two major Young Hegelians – Strauss and Bauer – remained within the bounds of Hegel’s idealist system. Strauss maintained that the evangelical legends resulted from a spontaneous, subconscious, mythological creativity on the part of the early Christian communities, an expression of the people’s spirit.

zh: 另一方面，鲍尔则认为《圣经》故事的起源在于某些杰出的宗教传道者的活动，他们有意识地创造了这些神话，而这些神话是人类自我意识历史发展中不可或缺的要素。鲍尔最终在与施特劳斯的论战中取得了胜利。他关于自我意识的主观唯心主义哲学成为了左派黑格尔主义的主要理论支柱。但本质上，一切都没有改变。施特劳斯和鲍尔虽然从不同的角度批评黑格尔，却始终未能摆脱唯心主义的基本立场。
en: On the other hand, Bauer sees the origin of the Bible stories in the activity of certain outstanding religious preachers, who consciously created the myths that constitute a necessary element in the historical development of human self-consciousness. Bauer finally emerged victorious from his polemics with Strauss. His subjective idealist philosophy of self-consciousness became the main theoretical plank of Left Hegelianism. But essentially, nothing had changed. Both Strauss and Bauer criticised Hegel from different points of view, but without ever breaking free from the basic ground of idealism.

zh: 左派黑格尔派的局限性
en: THE LIMITATIONS OF THE LEFT HEGELIANS

zh: 黑格尔哲学的革命性内涵早已隐含在左派黑格尔主义者的著作中，尽管表现得混乱且仍带有唯心主义色彩。为了将这一思想进一步发展，需要彻底的颠覆：完全摒弃唯心主义，转向唯物主义。但左派黑格尔主义者无力完成这一转变。事实上，他们正朝着完全相反的方向前进。黑格尔至少是一位客观的唯心主义者，其思想不仅深刻，而且在许多场合实际上接近现实。从黑格尔出发的出路——唯一可能的进步之路——就是唯物主义。
en: The revolutionary implications of Hegel’s philosophy were already implicit in the writings of the Left Hegelians, although in a confused and still idealist manner. In order to carry it any further, a complete overturn was required: the total abandonment of idealism and the transition to materialism. But the Left Hegelians were incapable of making that transition. In fact, they were moving in quite the opposite direction. Hegel at least was an objective idealist, whose thought was not merely profound but actually came close to reality on many occasions. The way forward from Hegel – the only possible path of advance – was materialism.

zh: 在试图建立一种与黑格尔相抗衡的理论时，左派黑格尔派陷入了极端主观主义的陷阱。主观唯心主义并不优于客观唯心主义，反而远逊于后者。它是所有哲学流派中最空洞、最肤浅、最无益的。而它却在整个二十世纪主导了所谓“哲学”的领域。左派黑格尔派著作的主要特征是极端个人主义，据此，历史的驱动力是“具有批判性思维的个体”。相比之下，他们将群众视为“精神的敌人”和进步的阻碍，对真正的社会或经济发展毫无概念。这使得他们所有的革命言论都沦为空洞的套话。
en: In attempting to erect an alternative to Hegel, the Left Hegelians fell into the trap of extreme subjectivism. Subjective idealism is not superior to objective idealism, but far inferior to it. It is the emptiest, most superficial and least rewarding of all schools of philosophical thought. And it has dominated what passes for philosophy for the whole of the twentieth century. The main characteristic of the writings of the Left Hegelians was extreme individualism, according to which the motive force of history was the ‘critically thinking individual’. By contrast, they regarded the masses as the ‘enemy of the spirit’ and progress, and had no notion of real social or economic development. This reduced all their revolutionary rhetoric to empty phrases.

zh: 他们的“批判”一方面使他们拒绝任何形式的基督教，另一方面则使他们接受了马克斯·施蒂纳在其著作《唯一者及其所有物》（Der Einzige und sein Eigentum）中倡导的一种极为奇特的哲学变体——“激进利己主义”。这是无政府主义的奠基文献之一，也是其与资产阶级个人主义之间关系的明确证明。本质上，这实际上仅仅是对自由主义（资产阶级）民主的一种理想化向往。
en: Their ‘critique’ led them, on the one hand, to a rejection of any form of Christianity and on the other hand, to a most peculiar variant of philosophy (‘radical egoism’) advocated by Max Stirner in his book Der Einzige und sein Eigentum (The Ego and its Own). This was one of the founding documents of anarchism and a clear proof of its relationship to bourgeois individualism. In essence, this was really only an idealised aspiration towards liberal (bourgeois) democracy.

zh: 但这堆听起来激进却混乱杂乱无章的思想，当进入一位名叫米哈伊尔·巴枯宁的年轻俄罗斯激进分子的脑海时，却产生了深远的影响——他宣称“破坏的喜悦本身就是一种创造性的喜悦”。这一混乱的思想学派完全是一条死胡同，到1844 年，它已不再作为一种连贯的力量而存在，尽管鲍尔的一些著作仍有些值得关注之处。黑格尔左派的破产最终在路德维希·费尔巴哈的著作中暴露无遗。
en: But this confused jumble of radical-sounding ideas had far-reaching effects when it entered the brain of a young Russian radical called Mikhail Bakunin, who proclaimed that “the joy of destruction in itself is a creative joy”. This confused school of thought was a complete dead-end, which, by 1844, had ceased to exist as a coherent force, although some of the writings of Bauer still provided something of interest. The bankruptcy of the Hegelian left was finally exposed in the writing of Ludwig Feuerbach.

zh: 路德维希·费尔巴哈
en: LUDWIG FEUERBACH

zh: 在黑格尔与马克思之间，矗立着路德维希·费尔巴哈（1804—1872）这一悲剧性人物。他是第一个从唯物主义立场挑战黑格尔的人。在《黑格尔哲学批判》中，他将黑格尔主义定性为“神学的最后避难所，最后的理性支柱”。
费尔巴哈出生于巴伐利亚的兰茨胡特，年轻时曾在海德堡攻读神学，但不到一年便放弃了，二十岁时前往柏林师从黑格尔学习哲学。他立刻被这位伟人所折服，成为了一名狂热的黑格尔主义者。后来，他成为埃尔朗根大学的哲学教授。
en: Between Hegel and Marx stands the tragic figure of Ludwig Feuerbach (1804-1872). He was the first one to challenge Hegel from a materialist standpoint. In his Critique of the Hegelian Philosophy, he characterised Hegelianism as “the last refuge, the last rational mainstay for theology.”

Born at Landshut in Bavaria, the young Feuerbach started to study theology in Heidelberg, but within a year abandoned it and, at the age of twenty, went to Berlin to study philosophy under Hegel. He immediately fell under the spell of the great man, and he became an ardent Hegelian. He later became a professor of philosophy at Erlangen.

zh: 尽管他被归类为“黑格尔左派”，但费尔巴哈对其空洞的言辞和抽象的唯心主义感到疏离，最终对整个思潮感到不满。他着手从唯物主义的立场出发，对黑格尔哲学进行彻底批判，并将黑格尔唯心主义描述为：“通过哲学来恢复一种已经丧失且消亡的基督教的最后一次宏大尝试”。
费尔巴哈正确地认识到，黑格尔唯心主义（实际上，所有唯心主义）的根源在于宗教：他写道：“近代哲学源于神学；它本身无非是神学被分解并转化为哲学。”
en: Although he was identified with the Hegelian Left, Feuerbach was alienated by its empty rhetoric and abstract idealism, and finally became dissatisfied with the whole business. He set out to make a thorough criticism of Hegel’s philosophy from the standpoint of materialism, describing Hegelian idealism as: “the last grand attempt to restore a lost and defunct Christianity through philosophy”.

Feuerbach correctly understood that the roots of Hegel’s idealism (in fact, of all idealism) lay in religion: “Modern philosophy”, he wrote, “proceeded from theology; it is itself nothing else but theology dissolved and transformed into philosophy”.

zh: 于是，他决定通过攻击宗教本身，用斧头砍向唯心主义的根源。他在《基督教的本质》一书中付诸了这一行动。这部划时代的著作于1841 年问世，产生了革命性的影响。费尔巴哈在《基督教的本质》中对宗教的唯物主义解读是一个重要的进步，为最终与唯心主义决裂指明了方向。该书当时产生的影响之大，难以言过其实。在同时代人眼中，他仿佛是普罗米修斯——那位敢于从众神那里偷取火并将其赐予人类的泰坦神。这标志着一场伟大的哲学革命。
en: And he decided to take an axe to the very roots of idealism by attacking religion itself. This he did in his book, The Essence of Christianity. The appearance of this epoch-making work in 1841 had revolutionary consequences. Feuerbach’s materialist reading of religion in The Essence of Christianity was an important step forward, pointing the way towards a final break with idealism. The impact it had at the time is difficult to overstate. To his contemporaries, he seemed like Prometheus, the Titan who dared to steal fire from the gods and give it to humans. This represented a great philosophical revolution.

zh: 他对年轻的马克思和恩格斯的影响尤为深远。恩格斯后来写道：“热情是普遍的：在那一瞬间，我们全都成了费尔巴哈主义者。”
唯独他愿意与黑格尔的唯心主义公开决裂。他大胆地以一种全新的视野——人类与自然统一的唯物主义学说——取代了旧有的神秘主义：
en: Especially great was his impact on the young Marx and Engels. Engels later wrote: “Enthusiasm was universal: we were all Feuerbachians for a moment.”

He alone was willing to carry out an open break with Hegel’s idealism. In place of the old mysticism, he boldly proclaimed an entirely new vision – the materialist doctrine of the unity of humankind and nature:

zh: 物质是理性的本质对象。如果没有物质，理性就不会有刺激，就没有思考的素材，因此也就没有内容。不能放弃物质而不放弃理性；不能承认物质而不承认理性。
en: Matter is an essential object for reason. If there was no matter, reason would have no stimulus and no material for thought and, hence, no content. One cannot give up matter without giving up reason; one cannot acknowledge matter without acknowledging reason.

zh: 他转向唯物主义的举措十分大胆。这需要极大的勇气，尤其是在当时欧洲普遍反动和普鲁士专制统治的背景下。这给年轻的马克思和恩格斯带来了启发。但最终，这一尝试还是失败了。费尔巴哈主要将人的意识视为自然的反映，同时强调人能够理解自身的本性及其与他人的关系。然而，归根结底，他的结论极其薄弱。他提出的对抗宗教统治的唯一替代方案是教育、道德、爱，甚至是一种新的宗教。
en: His move to materialism was a bold one. It required great courage, especially in the given context of general European reaction and the repressive Prussian state. It provided inspiration to the young Marx and Engels. But ultimately, it failed. Feuerbach regarded human consciousness mainly as a reflection of nature, while also stressing that man came to comprehend his own nature and his relations with other men. Ultimately, however, his conclusions are extremely weak. His only alternative to the domination of religion is education, morality, love, and even a new religion.

zh: 尽管费尔巴哈的唯物主义仍存在缺陷，使他无法进一步发展自己所发现的极具前景的前提，但他为辩证唯物主义这一革命性哲学指明了方向，该哲学最终由马克思和恩格斯所发展完善。起初，马克思和恩格斯深受费尔巴哈的影响。但很快，他们便意识到了他的不足。他们对费尔巴哈不愿从自己的思想中推导出所有结论的态度感到失望。他的著作，尤其是《基督教的本质》，在异化以及唯心主义与宗教之间的联系等问题上，包含着宝贵的见解。他对黑格尔辩证法的唯心主义性质提出了极其尖锐的批评。
en: Although Feuerbach’s materialism still suffered from defects that prevented him from developing the extremely promising premises that he had discovered, he pointed the way to the revolutionary philosophy of dialectical materialism, which was finally developed by Marx and Engels. At first, Marx and Engels were under the influence of Feuerbach. But very soon they became aware of his failings. They were disappointed by Feuerbach’s reluctance to draw all the conclusions from his own ideas. His writings, especially The Essence of Christianity, contain valuable insights on the subjects of alienation and the connection between idealism and religion. He was extremely critical of the idealist nature of Hegelian dialectics.

zh: 费尔巴哈让哲学从思辨的云端降临到人类层面——降临到那些源于自然、是自然不可分割组成部分的普通、物质的人身上。这是向前迈出的一步。但他的唯物主义无法回答它自己提出的问题。费尔巴哈哲学的核心是人。但费尔巴哈所理解的人，并非作为社会存在，而是作为抽象的个体。正因如此，这种哲学与现实中男女所处的真实世界几乎毫无关联。在费尔巴哈的著作中，真实的历史和真实的社会发展明显缺席。
en: Feuerbach made philosophy come down from the clouds of speculation to the human level – to normal, material human beings who are derived from nature and are an integral part of it. That was an important step forward. But his materialism was not capable of answering the questions that it posed. At the centre of Feuerbach’s philosophy is man. But Feuerbach takes man, not as a social being, but as an abstract individual. As such, this philosophy bore very little relation to the real world of men and women. Real history and real social development are conspicuous by their absence in the writings of Feuerbach.

zh: 尽管存在局限，《基督教的本质》因其对宗教的社会和历史根源所作的深刻洞见，至今仍具有相当大的研究价值。费尔巴哈将宗教视为人的异化，在此过程中，人的特质被对象化，并被视为超自然的存在。这仿佛是人患有一种人格分裂，并在上帝身上审视自身的本质。对费尔巴哈而言，异化的核心问题是宗教性的——在崇拜上帝时，人们实际上是在崇拜自己异化了的存在：
en: Despite its limitations, The Essence of Christianity still retains considerable interest for its brilliant insights into the social and historical roots of religion. Feuerbach regards religion as the alienation of man, in which human traits are made objective and treated as a supernatural being. It is as if man suffers from a kind of split personality, and contemplates his own essence in God. For Feuerbach, the central problem of alienation is religious – in worshipping God, men and women worship their own alienated being:

zh: 人——这就是宗教的奥秘——将自己的本质对象化，然后又使自己成为这个已化为主体、化为人格的对象化本质的对象。他成了另一个存在者的对象。
en: Man – and this is the secret of religion – objectifies his being, and then again makes himself the object of this objectified being, transformed into a subject, a person. He is an object to another being.

zh: 这一观点无疑是正确的，但完全忽略了所有异化的真正动力和根源——即在资本主义生产过程中，劳动以剩余价值的形式与其自身相异化。工人通过集体劳动创造了一种异化的力量——资本——它与工人对立并奴役他们。在费尔巴哈的著作中，“人”以片面、抽象且不真实的方式出现。真实的历史上的男女，只有在马克思主义哲学出现后才真正显现。
en: This idea was undoubtedly correct, but left completely out of account the real mainspring and origin of all alienation – the alienation of labour from itself in the form of surplus value in the process of capitalist production. Through their collective labour, the workers create an alien power – capital – which confronts them and enslaves them. In Feuerbach’s writings, Man appears in a one-sided, abstract and unreal manner. The real, historical men and women only appear with the advent of Marxist philosophy.

zh: 费尔巴哈及某些其他左派黑格尔主义者（如摩西·赫斯）的问题在于，他们仅仅对黑格尔说“不”，通过简单地否定黑格尔哲学来否定它。用德语的说法，他的主要错误就是“把婴儿和洗澡水一起倒掉”。在拒绝黑格尔哲学的同时，他也拒绝了其理性的核心——辩证法。这解释了费尔巴哈唯物主义的片面性，这也导致了它的失败。
en: The problem with Feuerbach and some other Left Hegelians (Moses Hess) is that he merely said no to Hegel, negating his philosophy by simply denying it. His main mistake was, to use the German expression, to throw the baby out with the bath water. In rejecting Hegel’s philosophy, he also rejected its rational core – dialectics. This explains the one-sided character of Feuerbach’s materialism, which caused its downfall.

zh: 费尔巴哈为其激进观点付出了沉重代价。他遭到了当局的残酷迫害。1830 年被大学解雇后，他在一个偏僻的村庄度过了晚年，成为一个悲剧性的、几乎被世人遗忘的人物。有人曾指出，任何语言中最令人悲伤的短语莫过于“本可以……”。对于费尔巴哈而言，这句话比对任何其他哲学家都更为贴切。他一生的大部分时光都在离群索居中度过，最终，他的命运就像一位哲学界的施洗约翰，是为他人铺平道路。他对唯物主义的捍卫，为马克思和恩格斯发起的哲学革命铺平了道路。他最重要的作用，就是作为这一新运动的催化剂。
en: Feuerbach paid a heavy price for his radical views. He was persecuted savagely by the authorities. Dismissed from the university in 1830, he spent his last years a tragic and virtually forgotten figure in an obscure village. Somebody once remarked that the saddest phrase in any language is ‘might have been’. This is truer of Feuerbach than any other philosopher. Having spent the greater part of his life in the wilderness, in the end, his destiny, like a philosophical John the Baptist, was to prepare the way for others. His defence of materialism paved the way for the philosophical revolution carried out by Marx and Engels. His most important role was to act as a catalyst for the new movement.

zh: 1848 年的革命将费尔巴哈和黑格尔左派的思想送入了历史的尘埃。那些曾经看似激进的思想，如今显得无关紧要。唯有马克思和恩格斯的革命纲领经受住了严峻考验。费尔巴哈并不理解这场革命，始终与马克思和恩格斯创立的新运动保持距离，尽管值得称道的是，他在晚年加入了德国社会民主党。
en: The revolution of 1848 consigned the ideas of Feuerbach and the Hegelian Left to oblivion. Ideas which had seemed radical before now appeared irrelevant. Only the revolutionary programme of Marx and Engels stood the test of fire. Feuerbach did not understand the revolution, and remained aloof from the new movement founded by Marx and Engels, although, to his credit, at the end of his life he joined the German Social Democratic Party.

zh: 一次非凡的合作
en: AN EXTRAORDINARY COLLABORATION

zh: 1844 年夏天，当我前往巴黎拜访马克思时，我们发现双方在所有理论领域都完全一致，我们的合作便始于那时。
en: When I visited Marx in Paris in the summer of 1844, our complete agreement in all theoretical fields became evident and our joint work dates from that time.

zh: 恩格斯这寥寥数语，标志着有史以来最著名且成果非凡的合作之一——卡尔·马克思与弗里德里希·恩格斯之间的合作——的开端。多年来，马克思主义的敌人（甚至包括一些自诩为马克思主义者的人）一直试图在这两位巨人之间制造隔阂。他们不择手段地“证明”，例如恩格斯在哲学领域所写的并非马克思的观点，诸如此类。
en: These few words by Engels mark the beginning of one of the most famous and extraordinarily fruitful collaborations of all time, the one between Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels. For many years, the enemies of Marxism (and even some who pretend to be Marxists) have attempted to drive a wedge between these two giants. They have tried by all manner of means to ‘prove’ that what Engels wrote, for example, in the field of philosophy, was not what Marx believed, and so on, and so forth.

zh: 哪怕只是粗略地阅读一下两人之间浩如烟海的书信往来，也能立即驳斥这种愚蠢的歪曲。这些书信填满了《马克思恩格斯全集》（英文版）中九卷厚重的卷册，时间跨度从1844 年一直延续到1883 年马克思逝世。这些书信充分展现了两人合作之紧密，以及他们如何共同构建和发展科学社会主义理论。由于马克思和恩格斯在所有理论问题上都极其严谨，两人绝不会对任何分歧置之不理。但其中根本找不到任何实质性的分歧。唯一的分歧仅出现在次要或战术性质的问题，例如美国内战中哪一方最终会取得胜利。
en: This stupid falsification is instantly disproved by even the most cursory reading of the voluminous correspondence between the two men, which fills nine bulky volumes of the Marx-Engels Collected Works (English edition), dating from 1844 right up to Marx’s death in 1883. These letters show just how closely the two men worked together, and how they jointly worked out and developed the theories of scientific socialism. Since both Marx and Engels were extremely scrupulous in all matters pertaining to theory, neither would ever allow any differences to pass without comment. But no serious differences are to be found. The only disagreement arose on questions of a secondary or tactical nature, such as which side would eventually emerge victorious in the American Civil War.

zh: 这些事情并未暴露出马克思和恩格斯之间在理论原则或方法论上存在任何严重分歧。他们的思想如此紧密地交织在一起，以至于马克思经常请恩格斯以他的（马克思的）名义撰写文章。这种紧密的合作——由一生的个人友谊所巩固——始于这两位年轻人满怀热情地投身于思想斗争之时：他们不仅与“青年黑格尔派”展开论战，同时也指出了费尔巴哈思想的局限性和缺陷。
en: Such matters did not reveal any serious differences between Marx and Engels, either on theoretical principles or methodology. So closely identified were their ideas that Marx often asked Engels to write articles in his (Marx’s) name. This close collaboration – cemented by a lifelong personal friendship – commenced when the two young men threw themselves eagerly into the battle of ideas, crossing swords with the Young Hegelians, but also pointing out the limitations and deficiencies of Feuerbach’s ideas.

zh: 马克思和恩格斯的联合阵线立即结出了硕果，即马克思主义哲学的奠基性著作之一《神圣家族，或对批判的批判所做的批判》的出版。该书写于1844 年9 月至11 月，于1845 年2 月首次出版，对左派黑格尔派给予了致命一击。
en: The united front of Marx and Engels immediately bore fruit with the publication of one of the seminal works of Marxist philosophy, The Holy Family, or the Critique of Critical Criticism, written between September and November 1844 and first published in February 1845. It dealt a mortal blow to the Left Hegelians.

zh: 马克思和恩格斯对左派黑格尔派的哲学思想进行了尖锐的批判，其中夹杂着最辛辣的讽刺。他们推翻了主观唯心主义的自我意识观念，阐明通过感官所感知到的现实，无论观察者的意识是否存在，都客观地存在着。他们指出，即使主体不在场进行感知，世界依然存在。这一点是大多数人毋庸置疑的。但哲学家本就是一类奇怪的人，而主观唯心主义者则比大多数人更奇怪。关于布鲁诺·鲍尔，他们写道，他“将自身之外的世界转化为一种现象，一种大脑中的纯粹幻想，随后又宣称这种幻想就是它的真实本质，即一种纯粹的幻想”。
en: Marx and Engels subjected the philosophical ideas of the Left Hegelians to a withering criticism, spiced with the most biting irony. They demolished the subjective idealist conception of self-consciousness, explaining that sensuously perceived reality exists irrespective of the consciousness of the observer. They pointed out that the world continues to exist even when the subject is not present to perceive it. That is something that most people accept without question. But philosophers are a strange breed, and the subjective idealists are stranger than most. Of Bruno Bauer, they wrote that he is “transforming the world outside himself into an appearance, a mere fancy of his brain, and afterwards declaring this fantasy to be what it really is, i.e., a mere fantasy”.

zh: 他们指出，主观唯心主义不可避免地会走向极端的个人主义，将个人英雄奉为历史的动力源泉，并轻蔑地否定群众作为历史主体所扮演的角色。对此他们写道：“批判的批判将整个人类归为一个没有灵魂的群体，这最鲜明地证明了，在思辨中，真实的人类是多么微不足道。”
1844 年8 月1 日，马克思就布鲁诺·鲍尔的月刊《文学报》致信费尔巴哈：
en: They pointed out that subjective idealism inevitably ended up in extreme individualism, the elevation of the individual hero as the mainspring of history, and a contemptuous rejection of the role of the masses as a historical agent. On this they wrote: “Critical criticism, by lumping humanity together in a spiritless mass, gives the most striking proof how infinitely small real human beings seem to speculation.”
On 1 August 1844, Marx wrote to Feuerbach about the Literatur-Zeitung, the monthly magazine of Bruno Bauer:
body.review: 底本正文写信日期为1844年8月1日，但原注12列作8月11日。两处各依底本保留。

zh: 在我那位相识多年的朋友——但如今已有些疏远——布鲁诺·鲍尔的批判性刊物《柏林文学报》中，他再次证明了德国人要摆脱这种对立的片面性是多么困难。我不知道你是否读过这本杂志。其中包含许多针对你的隐晦论战。
《文学报》的性质可归结为以下几点：“批判”被转化为一种先验的存在。这些柏林人并不把自己视为进行批判的人，而是视为批判者——只是碰巧不幸地身为人类。因此，他们只承认一种真实的需求，即理论批判的需求。因此，像蒲鲁东这样的人被指责为是以某种“实践”的“需求”作为出发点。这种批评因而沦为一种可悲且傲慢的唯智主义。意识或自我意识被视为人类唯一的品质。
en: In his critical Berlin Literatur-Zeitung, Bruno Bauer, my friend of many years standing – but now rather estranged – has provided fresh proof of how difficult it is for Germans to extricate themselves from the contrary one-sidedness. I don’t know if you have read the journal. It contains much covert polemic against you.

The character of the Literatur-Zeitung can be reduced to the following: “Criticism” is transformed into a transcendental being. These Berliners do not regard themselves as men who criticise, but as critics who, incidentally, have the misfortune of being men. They therefore acknowledge only one real need, the need of theoretical criticism. People like Proudhon are therefore accused of having made some “practical” “need” their point of departure. This criticism therefore lapses into a sad and supercilious intellectualism. Consciousness or self-consciousness is regarded as the only human quality.

zh: 马克思引用了鲍尔的观点，即哲学——或者更确切地说，用“青年黑格尔派”的术语来说，“批判”——不应流露情感或激情。鲍尔的原话是：
en: Marx quotes Bauer’s view that philosophy, or rather, ‘criticism’, to use the Young Hegelian jargon, should not display feeling or passion. Bauer says literally:

zh: 批评家既不应参与社会的苦难，也不应参与社会的欢乐；他既不应了解友谊和爱情，也不应了解仇恨和嫉妒；他应高坐于一片孤独之中，唯有奥林匹斯众神对世间颠倒错乱的嘲笑，偶尔从他的唇间回响。
en: The critic should participate neither in the sufferings nor in the joys of society; he should know neither friendship and love, nor hate and envy; he should be enthroned in a solitude, where only the laughter of the Olympian Gods over the topsy-turviness of the world resounds occasionally from his lips.

zh: 马克思接着说：
en: Marx goes on to say:

zh: 例如，爱情被否定，因为被爱者仅仅是一个“客体”。打倒客体！因此，这种批判自诩为历史中唯一的积极因素。它面对的是作为一个群体的整个人类——一个惰性的群体，其价值仅在于作为理性的对立面。因此，如果批评家流露情感或激情，便被视为最大的罪行；他必须是一个充满讽刺意味、冷若冰霜的智者。
en: Love, for example, is rejected because the loved one is only an “object”. Down with the object. This criticism thus regards itself as the only active element in history. It is confronted with the whole of humanity as a mass, an inert mass, which has value only as the antithesis of intellect. It is therefore regarded as the greatest crime if the critic displays feeling or passion, he must be an ironical ice-cold sophos.

zh: 对“批判的批判”的这一批判在《神圣家族》中得到了系统阐述，马克思和恩格斯在该书中证明，鲍尔的主观主义哲学只不过是将黑格尔《精神现象学》的基本思想推向了逻辑极致：实体必须升华为自我意识。
en: This criticism of ‘Critical Criticism’ is systematically developed in The Holy Family, where Marx and Engels prove that Bauer’s subjectivist philosophy merely carries to a logical end the basic idea of Hegel’s Phenomenology of Spirit: the substance must rise to self-consciousness.

zh: 科学社会主义的奠基者们摒弃了这些死气沉沉的抽象概念，而是以社会中真实的、物质的男女为出发点，以真实的历史为依据，而非唯心主义“自我意识”的精神世界。
en: Instead of these lifeless abstractions, the founders of scientific socialism proceeded from real, material men and women in society, real history, not the spirit world of idealist ‘Self-Consciousness’.

zh: 马克思的哲学革命
en: MARX’S REVOLUTION IN PHILOSOPHY

zh: 马克思的唯物主义与旧的机械论（“形而上学”）唯物主义毫无共同之处。事实上，它深受黑格尔思想的影响。但黑格尔将主体与客体之间的真实关系彻底颠倒了，而马克思则将这种关系重新倒转过来，使其再次牢牢立足于物质基础之上。
en: Marx’s materialism had nothing in common with the old mechanical (‘metaphysical’) materialism. In fact, it owed an immense debt to Hegel. But whereas the latter had turned the real relation between subject and object on its head, Marx inverted the relation, placing it once more with its feet firmly on material grounds.

zh: 1859 年8 月20 日，恩格斯在《人民报》第16 期上发表的一篇关于黑格尔的文章中，对卡尔·马克思所进行的哲学革命作了简短但极具启发性的阐述：
en: On 20 August 1859, in an article on Hegel in Das Volk, No. 16, Engels wrote a brief but highly illuminating account of the philosophical revolution carried out by Karl Marx:

zh: 自黑格尔去世以来，几乎没有人试图按照各门科学特有的内在逻辑来发展任何一门科学。官方的黑格尔学派只吸收了大师辩证法中最简单的手段，并将它们套用到一切事物上，往往表现得荒谬可笑。就他们而言，黑格尔的全部遗产仅限于一个简单的模板——借此可以正确地塑造任何主题——以及一串词语和短语，其唯一目的就是在缺乏思想和实证知识时，于恰当的时刻派上用场。因此，正如一位波恩大学教授所言，这些黑格尔主义者一无所知，却能对一切事物大书特书。事情最终就演变成了这样。尽管这些先生们自视甚高，但他们也足够清楚自己的弱点，因此尽可能地回避重大问题。旧式的迂腐学问凭借其优越的实证知识保住了阵地，随后随着费尔巴哈对思辨方法的摒弃，黑格尔主义逐渐沉寂，科学似乎又重新被那种拥有固定范畴的旧形而上学所支配……

因此，这里有一个亟待解决的问题，它与政治经济学本身并无直接关联。该如何对待科学？一方面是黑格尔留下的、相当抽象的“思辨”形式的黑格尔辩证法；另一方面则是普通且本质上属于沃尔夫学派的形而上学方法，这种方法再次盛行起来，并被资产阶级经济学家用来撰写那些冗长而杂乱的著作。该第二种方法早已被康德，尤其是黑格尔在理论上彻底驳倒，因此，它在实践中之所以仍被沿用，只能归因于惯性以及缺乏其他简单的替代方法。另一方面，黑格尔的方法以其现有的形式完全无法应用。它本质上是唯心主义的，而此处的任务却是构建一种比以往任何世界观都更具唯物主义色彩的世界观。黑格尔的方法以纯粹思想为出发点，而此处的出发点则必须是不可抗拒的事实。一种据其自身宣称“从无出发，经过无，达到无”的方法，以这种形态而言绝不合适。然而，在所有可用的逻辑材料中，它却是唯一至少可以作为出发点的要素。它未曾受到批判，也未曾被推翻；这位伟大辩证法家的任何反对者都未能在其宏伟的理论大厦上打开一道缺口。它之所以被遗忘，是因为黑格尔学派不知道如何运用它。因此，首先必须对黑格尔的方法进行彻底的批判。

黑格尔的思维方式之所以有别于所有其他哲学家，在于其背后蕴含着非凡的历史感。无论采用何等抽象和唯心主义的形式，他的思想发展始终与世界历史的发展并行不悖，而世界历史实际上被视为前者的证明。尽管这颠倒了实际的关系并将其彻底扭转，但真实的内容始终融入了他的哲学之中，尤其是因为黑格尔——与他的门生不同——并不依赖于无知，而是有史以来学识最渊博的思想家之一。他是第一个试图证明历史中存在发展、存在内在连贯性的人。无论他的历史哲学中的某些内容今天看来多么奇怪，其基本构想的宏伟气魄在今天看来依然令人钦佩，无论是与他的前辈相比，还是与那些在他之后敢于对历史提出普遍见解的后人相比。这一宏伟的历史观贯穿于《精神现象学》、《美学》和《哲学史》之中，其中的内容无处不在以历史的方式呈现，即使是以抽象且扭曲的形式，也始终置于明确的历史语境之中。
这一划时代的史观是新的唯物主义世界观的直接理论前提，而这本身也构成了与逻辑方法之间的纽带。既然即使从“纯粹思维”的角度来看，这种被遗忘的辩证法也已取得了如此成果，而且还轻而易举地应对了整个旧逻辑和形而上学，那么它无论如何都不可能仅仅是诡辩和吹毛求疵。但对这种方法的批判——整个官方哲学曾回避且至今仍在回避——绝非小事。
马克思是过去和现在唯一能够承担起这项工作的人：从黑格尔逻辑中提取包含黑格尔在此领域真正发现的核心，并将辩证法——剥离其唯心主义的外衣——确立为一种简明形式，使其成为思想发展的唯一正确方式。我们认为，马克思在《政治经济学批判》中所阐述的这一方法，其重要性丝毫不亚于其基本的唯物主义世界观。
en: Since Hegel’s death hardly any attempt has been made to develop any branch of science in its specific inner coherence. The official Hegelian school had assimilated only the most simple devices of the master’s dialectics and applied them to everything and anything, often with ridiculous incompetence. Hegel’s whole legacy was, so far as they were concerned, limited to a mere template, by means of which any subject could be shaped aright, and to a list of words and phrases whose only purpose was to turn up at the right moment, when ideas and positive knowledge were lacking. Thus it happened, as a professor at Bonn has said, that these Hegelians understood nothing but could write about everything. And that is what it came to. For all their conceit these gentlemen were, however, sufficiently conscious of their weakness to avoid major problems as far as possible. The old pedantic learning held its ground because of its superior positive knowledge, and then with Feuerbach’s renunciation of the speculative method, Hegelianism gradually fell asleep, and it seemed that science was once more dominated by the old metaphysics with its fixed categories…

Here there was, therefore, a question to be solved which was not connected with political economy as such. How was science to be dealt with? There was, on the one hand, the Hegelian dialectic in the quite abstract, “speculative” form in which Hegel had left it, and on the other hand the ordinary, essentially Wolffian, metaphysical method, which had again come into vogue and which was used by bourgeois economists to write their bulky rambling volumes. The second method had been theoretically so demolished by Kant and particularly by Hegel that its continued use in practice could only be rendered possible by inertia and the absence of an alternative simple method. The Hegelian method, on the other hand, was in its existing form quite inapplicable. It was essentially idealist, while the task here was to elaborate a world outlook more materialist than any previous one. Hegel’s method took as its point of departure pure thought, whereas here the starting point was to be inexorable facts. A method which, according to its own avowal, “came from nothing through nothing to nothing” was in this shape by no means suitable. It was, nevertheless, the only element among the entire available logical material which could at least serve as a point of departure. It had not been subjected to criticism, had not been overthrown; none of the opponents of the great dialectician had been able to make a breach in its proud edifice. It has been forgotten because the Hegelian school did not know how to apply it. Hence, it was first of all essential to subject the Hegelian method to thoroughgoing criticism.

What distinguished Hegel’s mode of thinking from that of all other philosophers was the exceptional historical sense underlying it. However abstract and idealist the form employed, the development of his ideas runs always parallel to the development of world history, and the latter is indeed supposed to be only the proof of the former. Although this reversed the actual relation and stood it on its head, yet the real content was invariably incorporated in his philosophy, especially since Hegel – unlike his pupils – did not rely on ignorance, but was one of the most erudite thinkers of all time. He was the first to try to demonstrate that there is development, an intrinsic coherence in history, and however strange some things in his philosophy of history may seem to us now, the grandeur of the basic conception is still admirable today, compared with either his predecessors or those who following him ventured to advance general observations on history. This monumental conception of history pervades the Phenomenology, the Aesthetics and the History of Philosophy, and the material is everywhere set forth historically, in a definite historical context even if in an abstract distorted manner.

This epoch-making conception of history was the direct theoretical precondition of the new materialist outlook, and already this constituted a connecting link with the logical method as well. Since, even from the standpoint of “pure thinking”, this forgotten dialectics had led to such results, and had moreover with the greatest ease coped with the whole of the former logic and metaphysics, there had, at all events, to be more to it than sophistry and hair-splitting. But criticism of this method, which the entire official philosophy had evaded and still evades, was no small matter.

Marx was and is the only one who could undertake the work of extracting from the Hegelian logic the kernel containing Hegel’s real discoveries in this field, and of establishing the dialectical method, divested of its idealist wrappings, in the simple form in which it becomes the only correct mode of the development of thought. The working out of the method which underlies Marx’s critique of political economy is, we think, a result hardly less significant than the basic materialist outlook.

zh: 《关于费尔巴哈的提纲》
en: THE THESES ON FEUERBACH

zh: 马克思早期著作中最重要的或许是《关于费尔巴哈的提纲》。这是在与费尔巴哈的片面的唯物主义决裂并开辟新方向的道路上迈出的重要一步。这寥寥数句浓缩的文字蕴含着一场哲学革命。让我们从第一条提纲开始：
en: Perhaps the most important of the early writings of Marx were the Theses on Feuerbach. They were an important step on the way to breaking with the one-sided materialism of Feuerbach and striking out in a new direction. These few concentrated sentences contain a philosophical revolution. Let us begin with the first thesis:

zh: 一切迄今为止的唯物主义（包括费尔巴哈的唯物主义）的主要缺陷在于：事物、现实、感性仅被理解为客体或观照的形式，而未被理解为感性的人类活动、实践，也未从主观角度加以理解。因此，与唯物主义相对，唯心主义抽象地提出了能动的一面——当然，唯心主义并不认识真实的、感性的活动本身。
en: The chief defect of all previous materialism (that of Feuerbach included) is that things, reality, sensuousness are conceived only in the form of the object, or of contemplation, but not as sensuous human activity, practice, not subjectively. Hence, in contradistinction to materialism, the active side was set forth abstractly by idealism – which, of course, does not know real, sensuous activity, as such.

zh: 马克思的这一句话常常引起某种困惑。其含义并非一目了然，除非将其置于哲学史的语境中，否则也无法阐明。然而，其中所蕴含的思想正是辩证唯物主义乃至整个马克思主义发展的出发点。
en: This phrase of Marx has often caused a certain puzzlement. Its meaning is not immediately clear, nor can it be made clear unless we place it in the context of the history of philosophy. Yet the idea contained within it is the starting point for the development of dialectical materialism, and of Marxism in general.

zh: 旧唯物主义之所以片面，在于它以静态、被动和沉思的方式看待人类思想。人仅仅是自然的观察者，记录“事实”：
en: The old materialism was one-sided in that it considered human thought in a static, passive and contemplative way. Man was merely an observer of nature, taking note of ‘the facts’:

zh: 在它看来，精神本身是空的，只是外部世界的镜子，是一个暗室，外部事物的影像投射其中，而精神本身既不作任何贡献，也不行动；其全部内容皆源于物质事物对其产生的印象。
en: The mind to it is in itself void, a mere mirror of the external world, a dark room into which the images of the things without fall, without any contribution or action on its part; its entire contents are due to the impressions made on it by material things.

zh: 早期的机械唯物主义无法解决这一问题，也无法对主体与客体之间的真实关系达成科学理解。这就是马克思在其《关于费尔巴哈的提纲》中所探讨的问题。早期的唯物主义受限于当时科学所达到的水平，而当时的科学本质上非常僵化且机械（恩格斯将其称为“形而上学的观点”，尽管今天我们对“形而上学”一词的用法有所不同）。
en: The early, mechanical materialism was unable to solve this problem and arrive at a scientific understanding of the real relationship between subject and object. This is what Marx deals with in his ‘Theses on Feuerbach’. The early materialism was limited by the level achieved by the science of the day, which was very rigid and mechanical in nature (Engels referred to it as the ‘metaphysical outlook’, although we use the word metaphysics differently today).

zh: 力学以简单化、静态且片面的方式看待主体与客体之间的关系：推、拉、举、惯性、杠杆、滑轮等。一切运动都由外部赋予。牛顿的机械宇宙需要全能者给予一推才能启动，但此后它便像钟表一样运转得完美无缺。这种关系是被动的、片面的。
en: Mechanics sees the relation between subject and object in a simplistic, static and one-sided way: pushing, pulling, lifting, inertia, levers, pulleys etc. All motion is imparted from without. Newton’s mechanical universe required the Almighty to give it a push to set it in motion, but after that it worked perfectly, like clockwork. The relationship was passive and one-sided.

zh: 在这个钟表般的宇宙中，主观活动和创造性主动性几乎没有或根本没有容身之地。每一项行动都由自然的永恒法则所预先决定。相比之下，唯心主义者则夸大了主体的作用，将其视为至关重要。他们甚至将客体的存在归因于主体。
en: In this clockwork universe, there is little or no room for subjective activity and creative initiative. Every action is predetermined by Nature’s Eternal Laws. By contrast, the idealists exaggerated the role of the subject, seeing it as all-important. They even derived the existence of the object from the subject.

zh: 客观唯心主义者黑格尔对主体活动的概念进行了总结和深化。这就是马克思所说的“主体要素是由唯心主义者而非唯物主义者所发展的”的含义。将这两个要素——即唯心主义者所主张的主体活动概念与物质世界的客观性观念——结合起来，才是解决这一问题的关键。
en: The conception of the activity of the subject was contained and developed by the objective idealist, Hegel. That is what Marx meant when he said that the subjective element was developed by the idealists, not the materialists. It was the bringing together of the two elements, the concept of activity of the subject of the idealists and the notion of the objectivity of the material world, which was the key to solving the problem.

zh: 第二条提纲
en: THE SECOND THESIS

zh: 人类思维能否被赋予客观真理，这不是一个理论问题，而是一个实践问题。人必须在实践中证明真理，即证明其思维的现实性、力量及其此岸性。关于脱离实践的思维是否真实的争论，是一个纯粹经院式的问题。
en: The question whether objective truth can be attributed to human thinking is not a question of theory but is a practical question. Man must prove the truth, i.e., the reality and power, the this-worldliness of his thinking in practice. The dispute over the reality or non-reality of thinking which is isolated from practice is a purely scholastic question.

zh: 几个世纪以来，认识论问题一直占据着哲学的核心地位。但所谓认识论问题，只有在将人类知识视为a）与肉体分离之物，以及b）与物质世界分离之物时，才会产生。
en: The problem of knowledge (epistemology) has occupied a central place in philosophy for centuries. But this so-called problem only arises when human knowledge is regarded a) as something separate from a physical body, and b) as something separate from the material world.

zh: 马克思和恩格斯揭露了唯心主义认识论根源中的错误前提。这实际上是一种欺骗手段：它首先将个别事物的普遍定义与其具体现实分离，然后进一步将这种普遍定义呈现为感官知觉对象的来源和第一因。
en: Marx and Engels exposed the false premises that lie at the roots of the epistemology of idealism. It is really a kind of swindle that begins by separating the general definition of individual things from their concrete reality and then proceeds to present the general definition as the source and the prime cause of the objects of sensory perception.

zh: 例如，将“水果”这一一般概念与真实的水果分离出来，并宣称它是梨、苹果和橙子的真正实体。从思辨唯心主义的立场来看，苹果、梨和橙子之间的区别无关紧要。但在现实生活中，情况却完全不是这样。没有人吃过抽象的“水果”，人们吃过的只有苹果、橙子等等。恩格斯指出，一位矿物学家如果只满足于宣称所有矿物都是“一般矿物”的变体，而不去研究它们真实的质的区别，“那他也就只是在想象中才算得上是矿物学家。”
en: For instance, the general concept ‘fruit’ is separated from real fruits, and declared to be the true substance of pears, apples and oranges. From the standpoint of speculative idealism, the distinction between apples, pears and oranges is immaterial. But in actual life, that is not at all the case. Nobody has ever eaten an abstract ‘fruit’, but only apples, oranges and so on. Engels pointed out that a mineralogist who confined himself to stating that all minerals are modifications of “the Mineral in general”, instead of studying their real qualitative distinctions, “would be a mineralogist only in his imagination.”

zh: 但这是否意味着抽象概念毫无价值，仅仅是我们想象力的任意产物呢？绝非如此！抽象思维是揭示自然奥秘、使人类能够征服自然的极有力的工具。在界定事物的本质时，我们可以揭示其隐藏的本质，即赋予事物特定身份的普遍特征。没有这种抽象的概括，理性思维便无从谈起。事实上，正如黑格尔所指出的，如果不将个别转化为普遍，就连最简单的句子（玛丽是个女人，这是一所房子，菲多是一只狗）都无法说出口。
en: But does that mean that abstractions are of no value, that they are merely the arbitrary products of our imagination? Not at all! Abstract thought is a most powerful tool for penetrating the secrets of nature and enabling human beings to gain mastery over it. In defining the nature of things, we can arrive at their hidden essence, the general traits that give them their specific identity. Without such abstract generalisations, rational thought would be impossible. In fact, as Hegel pointed out, it would be impossible even to utter the simplest sentence (Mary is a woman, this is a house, Fido is a dog) without turning a particular into a universal.

zh: 然而，思维中的抽象概念并非从天而降。它们最终都源于对物质事物的观察和对现实世界的体验，除非它们与真实的物质世界紧密对应，否则将毫无价值。这一过程历经了极其漫长的时间——事实上，如此漫长，以至于人类思维和语言的真正起源早已湮没在历史长河中。
en: Yet the abstractions of thought did not drop from the clouds. They are all ultimately derived from observation of material things and experience of the real world, and would have absolutely no value unless they closely corresponded to the real, material world. This process has taken place over a very long time – so long, in fact, that the real origins of human thought and language have long sunk into oblivion.

zh: 早在人类形成“圆”这一概念之前，他们就已经观察到了无数圆形物体：太阳、月亮、被截成两段的树干等等。通过这些观察，我们最终形成了“圆形”的观念，并由此产生了圆这一概念。没有人曾在现实生活中见过抽象的“圆”，因为这样的东西从来不存在，将来也不会存在。唯心主义者将抽象概念视为具有现实存在。对他们而言，物质世界不过是对“理念”的一种粗糙且不完美的模仿。实际上，情况恰恰相反。正如“伟大的定义者”亚里士多德很久以前指出的那样：“当然，脱离了具体的房屋，就不可能存在一般的房屋。”
en: Long before men and women developed the idea of a circle, they had observed a countless number of round objects: the sun, the moon, a tree trunk cut in half and so on. From these observations, eventually we arrive at the idea of ‘roundness’, and hence a circle. Nobody has ever seen an abstract circle in real life, because such a thing has never existed and never will exist. The idealists conceive of abstractions as if they had real existence. The material world for them is merely a crude and imperfect imitation of the Idea. In reality, it is the other way around. As Aristotle, ‘the great definer’, pointed out long ago: “But of course, there cannot be a house in general, apart from particular houses.”

zh: 黑格尔思想中的理性内核
en: THE RATIONAL KERNEL OF HEGEL

zh: 马克思和恩格斯将黑格尔对康德的批判推向了逻辑的极致——即与唯心主义彻底决裂。但与费尔巴哈全盘否定黑格尔思想不同，马克思和恩格斯认识到，黑格尔哲学中蕴含着一个非常重要的真理：辩证法。在黑格尔那里，辩证法仍被遮蔽，其深刻的真理隐藏在大量抽象而晦涩的推理之中。当黑格尔的辩证法摆脱了神秘主义和唯心主义的外衣，并建立在坚实的科学（唯物主义）基础上时，它便为一场真正的哲学革命提供了起点。
en: It was left to Marx and Engels to carry Hegel’s criticism of Kant to its logical conclusion – a complete break with idealism. But whereas Feuerbach rejected Hegel’s ideas in their totality, Marx and Engels understood that the Hegelian philosophy contained a very important truth: the dialectic. In Hegel, the dialectic remained obscured, its profound truths hidden in a mass of abstract and abstruse reasoning. Stripped of its mystical and idealist wrapping and placed on a sound scientific (materialist) basis, Hegel’s dialectic provided the starting point for a real philosophical revolution.

zh: 这需要马克思这样的天才，才能发现隐藏在黑格尔《逻辑学》篇章中的理性内核，并将其应用于真实的物质世界。他还阐明，费尔巴哈“人类学唯物主义”的缺陷在于，它将个人视为一个抽象实体。但真实的人类活动（劳动）并非孤立个体的活动，其本质必然是集体的。
en: It required the genius of a Marx to discover the rational kernel that lay hidden in the pages of Hegel’s Logic and apply it to the real, material world. He also explained that the deficiency of Feuerbach’s “anthropological materialism” is that here the individual is conceived of as an abstract entity. But real human activity (labour) is not the activity of isolated individuals. It is necessarily collective in its very essence.

zh: 主体与客体（思想与存在）之间的关系问题最终由马克思解决了，他指出，归根结底，所有哲学问题都在实践中得到解决：“关于脱离实践的思维是否真实的争论，是一个纯粹经院式的问题。”
唯物主义否定了“精神”、“意识”、“灵魂”等概念与物质相分离的观点。思想仅仅是大脑的一种存在方式，而大脑，就像生命本身一样，只是以某种方式组织起来的物质。精神就是我们所说的脑和神经系统活动的总和。但从辩证法的角度来看，整体大于部分之和。
en: The problem of the relation between subject and object (thought and being) was finally resolved by Marx, who pointed out that, ultimately, all the problems of philosophy are resolved in practice: “The dispute over the reality or non-reality of thinking which is isolated from practice is a purely scholastic question.”

Materialism rejects the notion that mind, consciousness, soul etc., is something separate from matter. Thought is merely the mode of existence of the brain, which, like life itself, is only matter organised in a certain way. Mind is what we call the sum total of the activity of the brain and the nervous system. But, dialectically, the whole is greater than the sum of the parts.

zh: 唯心主义者执意将意识描绘成一种“谜”，一种我们无法理解的东西。这种顽固地试图为凡人所能知晓的范围设定绝对界限的企图背后，潜藏着宗教迷信那阴暗的灵界，以及科学本应早在很久以前就将其送入博物馆的所有其他可悲的胡言乱语。尽管如此，科学仍在继续前进，逐一推翻所有陈旧的谜团，迫使宗教一步步退却，尽管宗教仍在高声抗议，声称自己有存在的权利。
en: The idealists persist in presenting consciousness as a ‘mystery’, something that we cannot comprehend. Hiding behind this stubborn attempt to place an absolute limit on what mere mortals are allowed to know lurks the murky spirit world of religious superstition and all the rest of the wretched mumbo-jumbo that science ought to have consigned to a museum long ago. Despite everything, science continues its onward march, tearing down one by one, all the old mysteries and forcing religion to retreat, step by step, loudly protesting its right to exist.

zh: 唯物主义观点与科学的结论高度契合，科学正在逐步揭示大脑的运作机制并揭开其奥秘。而人类发展的这一进程没有最终的界限。我们今天所不知道的，我们确信明天或后天定会知晓。唯物主义的最终真理，并非来自大学研讨室里的抽象辩论，而是来自社会发展和科学史。人类不仅只是观照自然，而且积极地改造自然，而这种永无止境的生产活动，正是检验思想正确与否的标准，正如恩格斯所解释的：
en: The materialist view corresponds closely to the conclusions of science, which is gradually uncovering the workings of the brain and revealing its secrets. And there is no final limit to this process of human development. What we do not know today, we are sure we shall know tomorrow, or the day after tomorrow. The final truth of materialism is provided, not by abstract debates in university seminar rooms, but by social development and the history of science. Humankind does not merely contemplate nature but actively transforms it, and this ceaseless productive activity is what demonstrates the correctness or otherwise of ideas, as Engels explains:

zh: 对这一观点以及所有其他哲学怪论最具说服力的反驳就是实践，即实验和工业。如果我们能够通过亲手引发某种自然现象、在其条件下将其产生，并顺便使其为我们的目的服务，从而证明我们对该现象的认识是正确的，那么康德那难以捉摸的“物自体”就彻底终结了。在动植物体内产生的化学物质，一直都是这样的“物自体”，直到有机化学开始逐一合成它们为止，此后，“物自体”便成为了为我之物……
en: The most telling refutation of this as of all other philosophical quirks is practice, namely, experimentation and industry. If we are able to prove the correctness of our conception of a natural phenomenon by bringing it about ourselves, producing it out of its conditions and making it serve our own purposes into the bargain, then the ungraspable Kantian “thing-in-itself” is finished. The chemical substances produced in the bodies of plants and animals remained just such “things-in-themselves” until organic chemistry began to produce them one after another, whereupon the “thing-in-itself” became a thing for us…

zh: 主观唯心主义
en: SUBJECTIVE IDEALISM

zh: 当我们进入主观唯心主义阶段时，情况变得更加复杂。这一思潮随着贝克莱和休谟的出现而形成明确的趋势，并延续到康德的哲学中，在那里它继续引发无尽的混乱。康德是一位卓有声望的哲学家。他的巨大功绩在于对传统逻辑形式进行了彻底的批判。但他的致命弱点在于他在认识论上的主观主义立场——不幸的是，这一立场正是他从庸俗经验论者大卫·休谟那里继承而来的。
en: A further complication arises when we reach the stage of subjective idealism, which emerged as a definite trend with Berkeley and Hume and passed into the philosophy of Kant, where it continued to cause endless confusion. Kant was a philosopher of stature. His great merit was to subject the traditional forms of logic to a thoroughgoing criticism. But his Achilles’ heel was to be found in his subjectivist position on the theory of knowledge, which he unfortunately took over from the vulgar empiricist David Hume.

zh: 这正是他主要弱点——模棱两可、前后矛盾和不可知论——的根源。如前所述，康德在揭示传统逻辑局限性的同时，却未能与其彻底决裂，结果使自己陷入了各种无法解决的矛盾（二律背反），而他最终也未能解决这些问题。在康德的认识论中，我们看到一种对意识的片面看法，它被呈现为一道屏障，据称将我们与“外部”世界隔绝开来。事实上，我们是这个世界的一部分，并非与之分离，而意识并非将我们与世界隔绝，而是将我们与之联系在一起。人类与物质世界的关系从一开始就不是观照的，而是能动的。正如德国伟大诗人歌德所言：“Am anfang war die Tat！”——起初是行动！
en: Here was the source of his main weaknesses – ambiguity, inconsistency and agnosticism. As has been explained, in failing to make a clean break with the traditional logic, while exposing its limitations, Kant landed himself in all kinds of insoluble contradictions (antinomies), which he left unresolved. In Kant’s theory of knowledge we have a one-sided view of consciousness, which is presented as a barrier that is supposed to shut us off from the ‘external’ world. In fact, we are part of this world, not separate from it, and consciousness does not separate us but connects us to it. The relationship of humans to the physical world from the very beginning was not contemplative but active. As the great German Poet Goethe said: “Am anfang war die Tat!” – In the beginning was the Deed!

zh: 我们不仅用大脑思考，更用整个身体思考。思考不应被视为一种孤立的活动（正如吉尔伯特·赖尔对勒内·笛卡尔“心灵与身体”二元论的讽刺性描述——“机器中的幽灵”）
，而应被视为整个人类体验的一部分，是人类感性活动以及与世界和他人互动的一部分。思考行为必须被视为这一复杂且持续互动过程的一部分，而非机械地并列于其旁的孤立活动。伟大的天才黑格尔曾接近发现这一真理，但尽管他拥有巨大的智力，却未能从理论到实践实现决定性的飞跃，因为他被自己的唯心主义先入之见蒙蔽了双眼。
en: We do not only think with our brain, but with our whole body. Thinking must be seen, not as an isolated activity (“the ghost in the machine”, as Gilbert Ryle caricatured René Descartes’ dualist theory of mind and body)

but as part of the whole human experience, of human sensuous activity and interaction with the world and with other people. The act of thinking must be seen as part of this complex process of permanent interaction, not as an isolated activity that is mechanically juxtaposed to it. The great genius Hegel came close to discovering the truth, but despite his colossal intellectual power, he failed to make the decisive leap from theory to practice, blinded as he was by his idealist preconceptions.

zh: 康德的主观唯心主义曾被黑格尔从客观唯心主义的立场上彻底推翻。但在这位伟人去世后，它又卷土重来，并自此以来，以各种伪装的形式，一直是资产阶级哲学的主流趋势。马克思在《关于费尔巴哈的提纲》的第二条中，对此给出了决定性的驳斥。只有当我们站在实践的立场上，从具体的、历史的视角来探讨认识论，而不是从空洞而静止的抽象立场上出发，才能彻底驳斥主观唯心主义的论点以及主体-客体问题。
en: Kant’s subjective idealism had been thoroughly demolished by Hegel from the standpoint of objective idealism. But it raised its head once more after the death of the great man and, in one disguise or another, has been the dominant trend in bourgeois philosophy ever since. It received a definitive answer in the second of Marx’s ‘Theses on Feuerbach’. The arguments of subjective idealism and the subject-object problem can only be thoroughly demolished when we adopt the standpoint of practice and approach the theory of knowledge from a concrete historical point of view, and not from the standpoint of empty and static abstraction.

zh: 这种辩证观念的雏形在黑格尔那里就已经存在了。马克思所做的，就是剥去其唯心主义的外衣，并以清晰而科学的方式加以阐述。黑格尔在《哲学史》中说：“精神的存在就是它的活动，而它的活动就是对自身的认识。”但在黑格尔那里，思考不仅仅是一种沉思活动。他所称的“理性”——即思维的最高形式——不仅接受既定事实，而且对它们进行加工和转化。
en: In embryo, the elements of this dialectical conception are already present in Hegel. What Marx did was strip it of its idealist disguise, and express it in a clear and scientific manner. Hegel says in The History of Philosophy that “the being of mind is its act, and its act is to be aware of itself.” But in Hegel, thinking is not merely a contemplative activity. The highest form of thought, which he calls Reason, does not merely accept the given facts, but works upon them and transforms them.

zh: 在黑格尔那里，思想与存在之间、“主体”与“客体”之间的矛盾，是通过认识过程本身得以克服的，这种过程不断深入地渗透到客观世界之中。然而，在黑格尔的理论中，我们看到的不是真实的人，而是“自我意识”这一抽象概念。历史力量的真实斗争，被表述为思想斗争的虚幻形式。若不彻底决裂于黑格尔唯心主义，便不可能取得进一步的进步。马克思和恩格斯在与费尔巴哈的抽象唯物主义决裂后，完成了这一转变。
en: The contradiction between thought and being, between ‘subject’ and ‘object’, is overcome in Hegel through the process of knowledge itself, which penetrates ever deeper into the objective world. In Hegel, however, instead of genuine human men and women we have the abstraction of Self-Consciousness. The real struggle of historical forces is expressed in the shadowy form of the struggle of ideas. No further progress was possible without a complete break with Hegelian idealism. This transition was accomplished by Marx and Engels after their break with the abstract materialism of Feuerbach.

zh: “革命的代数”
en: THE ‘ALGEBRA OF REVOLUTION’

zh: 19 世纪俄罗斯革命民主主义者亚历山大·赫尔岑曾将辩证法描述为“革命的代数”。
当马克思和恩格斯将黑格尔哲学中理性的核心从其唯心主义的牢笼中解放出来时，他们便将辩证法转化为革命行动的强大武器：
en: The nineteenth century Russian revolutionary democrat Alexander Herzen once described the dialectic as the “algebra of revolution”.
When Marx and Engels freed the rational kernel of Hegel’s philosophy from its idealist prison, they transformed dialectics into a powerful weapon for revolutionary action:

zh: 因此，辩证法归结为一门研究外部世界和人类思维的普遍运动规律的科学——这两套规律在实质上是一致的，但在表现形式上有所不同：人类思维能够有意识地运用这些规律，而在自然界中，以及迄今为止人类历史的大部分时期，这些规律则以外部必然性的形式，在无尽的一系列看似偶然的事件中无意识地显现出来。由此，概念的辩证法本身仅仅成为了现实世界辩证运动的自觉反映，黑格尔的辩证法因此被“倒置”了；或者更确切地说，是被从它原本所立的“头”上移开，置于“脚”上。而这种唯物辩证法，多年来一直是我们最好的劳动工具和最锋利的武器……
en: Thus dialectics reduced itself to the science of the general laws of motion, both of the external world and of human thinking – two sets of laws which are identical in substance, but differ in their expression in so far as the human mind can apply them consciously, while in nature and also up to now for the most part in human history, these laws assert themselves unconsciously, in the form of external necessity, in the midst of an endless series of seeming accidents. Thereby the dialectic of concepts itself became merely the conscious reflex of the dialectical motion of the real world and thus the Hegelian dialectic was placed upon its head; or rather, turned off its head, on which it was standing, and placed upon its feet. And this materialist dialectic, which for years was our best means of labour and our sharpest weapon…

zh: 《关于费尔巴哈的提纲》第三条
en: THE THIRD THESIS ON FEUERBACH

zh: 马克思在《关于费尔巴哈的提纲》第三条中写道：
en: In his third thesis on Feuerbach, Marx wrote:

zh: 关于环境变化和教育的唯物主义学说，却忘记了环境是由人改变的，而且教育者本身也必须接受教育。因此，这种学说必须将社会分为两部分，其中一部分凌驾于社会之上。
环境改变与人类活动或自我改变的重合，只有作为革命实践才能被构想和理性地理解。
en: The materialist doctrine concerning the changing of circumstances and upbringing forgets that circumstances are changed by men and that the educator must himself be educated. This doctrine must, therefore, divide society into two parts, one which is superior to society.
The coincidence of the changing of circumstances and of human activity or self-change can be conceived and rationally understood only as revolutionary practice.

zh: 在这里，思想终于与活动结合在一起——不是学者那种片面的、纯粹的智力活动，而是真实、感性的人类活动。但这不可避免地将我们引向革命性的结论。从唯物主义的立场来看，男女的发展是由其存在的物质条件决定的。这实际上是一个不言而喻的命题，即使我们考虑到遗传因素——它无疑在这种发展中起着一定作用。
en: Here at last thought is united with activity – not the one-sided purely intellectual activity of the scholar but real, sensuous human activity. But this inevitably leads us to revolutionary conclusions. From the standpoint of materialism, the development of men and women is determined by the material conditions of their existence. This is really a self-evident proposition, even when we take into consideration the genetic element that undoubtedly has a role to play in this development.

zh: 出生时的生物学偶然性为个体男女的体质和智力发展提供了基本原料。但最终决定这种发展进程的，是客观环境。阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦是一位天才，不能排除这样一种可能性：无论其生活条件如何，他的天才迟早都会以某种方式展现出来。但如果他出生在印度某个村庄，是无地劳动者的儿子，他的天才能否充分发挥其全部潜力呢？他或许能在种稻方面掌握令人印象深刻的技艺，甚至可能晋升为村里的手工艺人。也许会，也许不会。但他会提出那项彻底改变二十世纪科学的相对论吗？这个问题不言自明。仅仅断言物质条件决定着人们的生活，并不能穷尽问题的全部。如果群众的物质条件构成了一道无法逾越的障碍，阻碍了数以百万计的人实现作为人类的真正潜能，如果它扼杀了存在于每个人身上、或多或少的创造火花，那么这些客观条件就必须加以改变。
en: The biological accidents of birth provide the basic raw material for the physical and mental development of individual men and women. But it is objective circumstances that will ultimately decide the way in which this development proceeds. Albert Einstein was a genius, and it is not excluded that his genius would have sooner or later expressed itself in one way or another, independently of the conditions of his life. But if he had been born the son of a landless labourer in an Indian village, would his genius have realised its full potential? He may have acquired an impressive level of skills in the planting of rice or perhaps even risen to the rank of a village artisan. Maybe, or maybe not. But would he have developed the theory of relativity that transformed science in the twentieth century? The question answers itself. The mere assertion that material conditions determine the lives of men and women does not exhaust the matter. If the material conditions of the masses constitute an insuperable obstacle that prevents millions of people from realising their true potential as human beings, if it suffocates that creative spark that exists in every individual, to one extent or another, then it follows that these objective conditions must be changed.

zh: 改革派为反驳革命思想而经常提出的论点是，必须“教育群众”。有时甚至会听到所谓的“马克思主义者”表达这一谬论的变体。他们试图以群众所谓的“不成熟”来解释为何尚未发生成功的社会主义革命——声称群众尚不配进行革命，大概是因为他们还没读完马克思的三卷本《资本论》！为了取得成功，工人必须聚集在宗派分子的讲台周围，由他们来“教育”工人，并最终向工人颁发一份“成熟证书”。凭借这份庄严的文件，群众便可以在第二天早上九点整夺取政权。
en: The argument that is frequently advanced by reformists to counter the idea of revolution is that it is necessary to ‘educate the masses’. Sometimes one even hears a variant of the same false idea expressed by so-called Marxists. They try to explain the absence of a successful socialist revolution by referring to the alleged ‘immaturity’ of the masses, who are not yet worthy to carry out a revolution, presumably because they have not yet read the three volumes of Marx’s Capital! In order to succeed, the workers must gather round the rostrum of the sectarians who will ‘educate’ them and eventually present them with a Certificate of Maturity. Armed with this portentous document, the masses could then proceed to take power the very next morning at precisely nine o’clock.

zh: 针对这种荒谬的胡言乱语，马克思机智地指出：需要这种证书的不是群众，恰恰是那些“教育者”自己才需要接受教育。这些诡辩论调不过是对现状的一种狡猾而玩世不恭的辩护。因为正是资本主义制度下的客观生活条件，构成了阻隔广大民众获取文化的不可逾越的屏障。
en: Answering this ridiculous nonsense, Marx pointed out wittily, it is not the masses who need such a certificate, but precisely the ‘educators’ who need educating. These sophistical arguments are merely a cunning and cynical defence of the status quo. For it is precisely the objective conditions of life under capitalism that constitute an impenetrable barrier between the mass of the population and access to culture.

zh: 社会被划分为“思想家”和“行动者”，《圣经》将后者描述为“砍柴的和打水的”。
对体力劳动的蔑视既反映了资产阶级的偏见，也是试图为资产阶级社会的结构、道德和价值观辩护——在这个社会里，据称“自我”（即“个人”）至高无上。人类历史的驱动力被描绘为个体主角的行动与意志，无论他们是英雄还是恶棍。
en: Society is divided into ‘thinkers’ and ‘doers’, which the Bible describes as “the hewers of wood and the drawers of water.”

Contempt for manual labour is at once a reflection of bourgeois prejudice and an attempt to justify the structures, morals and values of bourgeois society, a society in which the Ego (the ‘individual’) is said to rule supreme. The mainspring of human history is presented as the actions and volition of individual protagonists, whether heroes or villains.

zh: 然而实际上，绝大多数人的个性被压制，沦为极少数人的奴隶——这极少数人拥有并控制着生产资料，从而掌握着生命本身的关键。而且说句实话，就连这一少数群体也受制于他们无法掌控的力量。尽管创造社会财富的群众构成了人类的压倒性多数，但他们没有历史，也没有名字；他们的声音被压制，他们的存在大多被忽视。一万多年来，社会一直被极少数特权阶层所支配，他们垄断了文化。
en: In reality, however, the individuality of the great majority is crushed and enslaved to the individuality of a tiny handful that own and control the means of production and thus the key to life itself. And to tell the whole truth, even this minority is subject to forces that they do not control. Although the masses who create the wealth of society make up the overwhelming majority of humankind, they have no history and no name; their voices are silenced and their existence largely ignored. For over 10,000 years, society has been dominated by a tiny privileged minority that has held in its hands a monopoly on culture.

zh: 马克思指出，社会存在决定意识。要改变人，就必须改变他们的生存条件。但社会该如何改变？这才是关键问题！社会的根本变革无法通过被动的沉思，也无法通过大学哲学系里无休止的思辨讨论来实现，而只能依靠被压迫群众自身的集体革命行动。而且，群众不是从书本上学习，而是从阶级斗争的具体经验中学习。
en: Marx explained that social being determines consciousness. In order to change people, it is necessary to change their conditions of existence. But how is society to be changed? That is the question! A fundamental change in society cannot be achieved by passive contemplation or endless speculative discussions in the philosophy departments of universities, but only by the collective revolutionary action of the oppressed masses themselves. And the masses do not learn from books, but from the concrete experience of the class struggle.

zh: 《关于费尔巴哈的提纲》第八条：迈向《共产党宣言》
en: THE EIGHTH THESIS ON FEUERBACH: TOWARDS THE COMMUNIST MANIFESTO

zh: 一切社会生活在本质上都是实践的。所有使理论陷入神秘主义的谜团，都在人类实践以及对这种实践的理解中找到了合理的解决之道。
en: All social life is essentially practical. All mysteries which lead theory to mysticism find their rational solution in human practice and in the comprehension of this practice.

zh: 这些话标志着与过去的决定性决裂。它们承认有必要发展一种全新的思维方式：一种新型的哲学，实际上是一种非哲学的理论。
en: These words represent a decisive break with the past. They are a recognition of the need to develop an entirely new way of thinking: a new type of philosophy that was, in effect, a non-philosophical theory.

zh: 从唯物主义的角度来看，思维并非一种孤立的活动，而是与人类的整体存在密不可分。马克思指出，劳动——即物质生产——是人的类生活。也就是说，劳动是人类的存在方式。人类与动物的这一特定区别并非天生的，而是贯穿整个人类历史的生产过程中产生并发展的，从制作第一把粗糙的石斧，到制造计算机、机器人以及进行太空旅行。
en: From a materialist point of view, thinking is not an isolated activity, but is inseparable from human existence in general. Marx says that labour, material production, is man’s species-life. That is to say, labour is the mode of existence of human beings. This specific distinction of man from animal is not a natural one, but emerges and develops in the process of production throughout human history, from the fashioning of the first crude stone axes to the building of computers, robots and space travel.

zh: 人类通过具体的、感性的活动发展思想——这不仅是智力活动，更是集体的人类劳动。通过劳动改造物质世界，人们同时也改造着自己，并在此过程中发展和拓展了思维的视野。劳动的力量在于无数个体的努力、奋斗和创造力的结合。正是这种神奇的结合，造就了文明的一切奇迹。
en: Humankind develops thought through concrete, sensuous activity – not merely intellectual activity, but collective human labour. By transforming the material world through labour, men and women also transform themselves and, in so doing, develop and extend the horizon of their thinking. The power of labour lies in the combination of the efforts, strivings and creativity of a vast number of individual men and women. It is this magical combination that gives rise to all the wonders of civilisation.

zh: 在人类劳动的力量中，我们看到了黑格尔所称的“特殊与普遍的统一”的具体体现。然而，这种必要的统一却一直遭到顽固的否认。人类的思想和行动并非被呈现为一种集体活动，而是被视为孤立个体的作为。这种片面观点的背后，隐藏着一种根深蒂固的偏见：它将脑力劳动奉为人类进步中最重要的——甚至可以说是唯一的——要素，而将体力劳动的作用贬低到微不足道的地步。
en: In the power of human labour, we see the concrete realisation of what Hegel called the unity of the Particular and the Universal. Yet this necessary unity has been stubbornly denied. The thoughts and actions of humankind are presented, not as a collective activity, but as the work of isolated individuals. Behind this one-sided view lies a deep-seated prejudice that elevates mental labour to the most important, if not the sole element in human progress, while the role of manual labour is relegated to insignificance.

zh: 一个阶级对另一个阶级的奴役并非源于资本主义。数千年来，它以各种形式存在，马克思和恩格斯在其关于历史唯物主义的著作中对此进行了详尽的探讨。这一理论的轮廓在《德意志意识形态》（尤其是题为“费尔巴哈”的第一章）中已初见端倪。这一理论最终以成熟的形式出现在世界历史上最伟大、最具影响力的文献之一——《共产党宣言》中。该宣言首次将人类历史置于科学基础上，开篇便提出了一个大胆的论断：“迄今为止一切社会历史，都是阶级斗争的历史”。
en: The enslavement of one class by another does not originate with capitalism. It has existed in different forms for thousands of years, a fact that Marx and Engels examined in great detail in their writings on historical materialism. The outlines of this theory are already seen in The German Ideology (notably in the first chapter entitled ‘Feuerbach’). It finally emerges in a finished form in one of the greatest and most influential documents in world history: The Communist Manifesto, which for the first time places human history on a scientific basis, starting with a bold statement: “The history of all hitherto existing society is the history of class struggles”.

zh: 该文以一段振聋发聩的宣言作结：
en: And it ends with a stirring proclamation:

zh: 让统治阶级在共产主义革命面前颤抖吧！无产者失去的只是锁链，他们将赢得整个世界。全世界的工人，联合起来！
en: Let the ruling classes tremble at a communistic revolution. The proletarians have nothing to lose but their chains. They have a world to win. Workers of All Countries, Unite!

zh: 一个衰落的时期
en: A PERIOD OF DECLINE

zh: 在过去一个半世纪里，哲学领域犹如一片荒芜的沙漠，仅偶有生命迹象。巨人的时代已悄然消逝。过去的宝库——连同其古老的荣光与智慧的闪光——已不复存在。它的火焰已彻底熄灭。这片仍自称“哲学”的荒漠，如今栖息着一群太监和争吵不休的侏儒。在这片思想荒原上，人们无论如何寻找，都找不到任何启迪之源。现代资产阶级哲学的彻底空洞，甚至连哲学家们自己也日益察觉到了这一点。彼得·昂格曾在纽约大学担任著名分析哲学家数十年，师从该学派的宗师A. J. 艾耶尔。他最终得出了什么结论？
en: For the past one-and-a-half centuries, the realm of philosophy has resembled an arid desert with only the occasional trace of life. The age of giants has passed away without trace. The treasure trove of the past, with its ancient glories and flashes of illumination, has vanished. Its fire is utterly extinguished. This desert that still calls itself philosophy is inhabited by a tribe of eunuchs and squabbling pygmies. In this intellectual wasteland one would search in vain for any source of illumination. The complete emptiness of modern bourgeois philosophy is something that has been increasingly noted, even by the philosophers themselves. Peter Unger spent decades working as a celebrated analytic philosopher at the University of New York, having been tutored by the guru of that philosophy, A. J Ayer. What conclusion did he finally draw?

zh: 2014 年，他出版了一本题为《空洞的思想：对分析哲学的批判》的著作，书名颇为耐人寻味。在一篇为该书辩护的文章中，他指出：
en: In 2014 he published a book with the interesting title, Empty Ideas: A Critique of Analytic Philosophy. In an article defending the book, he states the following:

zh: ［在］过去的五十年里，几乎没有出现过任何新的思想，其真伪对具体现实中事物的本质有何影响或意义——除了无数极其狭隘的思绪，那些无非是关于“哪些人使用哪些词语”以及“这些人如何使用他们的词语”的观念——而其深度也仅止于此。
en: [D]uring the last five decades, there has been offered hardly any new thoughts whose truth, or whose untruth, makes or means any difference as to how anything ever is as concern [sic] concrete reality, except for ever so many perfectly parochial thoughts, ideas about nothing much more than which words are used by which people, and how various of these people use these words of theirs – and nothing any deeper than that.

zh: 我只想补充一点：现代资产阶级哲学的其他所有产物也同样如此，而且这种情况持续的时间远不止五十年。
en: I would only add that the same thing can be said of every other product of modern bourgeois philosophy, and for a period considerably longer than five decades.

zh: 这种对词语含义的无休止的语义钻牛角尖和纠缠，就像一只永不厌倦地追逐自己尾巴的狗。这让人联想到中世纪经院哲学家那些曲折离奇的辩论——他们无休止地争论天使的性别，以及有多少个天使能站在针尖上跳舞。很难说哪一种更糟：是所谓后现代主义那令人无法忍受的故作高深，还是其内容显而易见的空洞。这种乏味的文字游戏竟然能被冠以“哲学”之名，恰恰证明了现代资产阶级思想已经堕落到何种地步。
en: The constant semantic fiddling and fussing about the meaning of words resembles a dog that never tires of chasing its own tail. It calls to mind the convoluted debates of the medieval Schoolmen who argued endlessly over the sex of angels, and how many can dance on the head of a pin. It is hard to say what is worse: the intolerable pretensions of so-called postmodernism, or the obvious emptiness of its content. The fact that this tedious playing with words could be given the name of philosophy at all is proof of how far modern bourgeois thought has declined.

zh: 黑格尔在《精神现象学》中写道：“从人类精神所满足的微不足道之事，我们可以判断其损失的程度。”这句名言堪称黑格尔和费尔巴哈之后所有资产阶级哲学的恰当墓志铭。资产阶级哲学早已步入衰老阶段，只能发出语无伦次的呓语，不断乏味地重复那些老生常谈，这些陈词滥调除了引发烦躁和厌倦之外，已无法激起任何反应。用莎士比亚的话来说：无牙、无眼、无味，一无所有。
en: Hegel wrote in the Phenomenology: “By the little with which the human spirit is satisfied, we can judge the extent of its loss.” That would be a fitting epitaph for all the bourgeois philosophy after Hegel and Feuerbach. Bourgeois philosophy has long ago entered into the stage of senility where it is only capable of incoherent babbling and constant wearisome repetition of old stories that no longer evoke any reaction other than a sense of irritation and boredom. It is, to quote Shakespeare: Sans teeth, sans eyes, sans taste, sans everything.

zh: 哲学的终结
en: THE END OF PHILOSOPHY

zh: 新精神的开端是各种文化形式中广泛革命的产物，是复杂而曲折的旅程以及同样巨大而艰辛的努力所带来的回报。开端就是从相继展开和广泛展开中回归自身的整体，是由此形成的整体的简单概念。但这个简单整体的现实性在于：这些已然成为环节的形态再次发展并取得新的形态，但如今在它们新的元素中，在已经显现的意义上。
en: The beginning of the new spirit is the product of a wide-ranging revolution in various forms of culture, the reward of a complicated, tortuous journey and of an equally immense and strenuous effort. The beginning is the whole that has returned into itself from succession as well as extension, the resultant simple concept of the whole. But the actuality of this simple whole consists in this: these configurations that have become moments again develop anew and take on a configuration, but now in their new element, in the sense that has emerged.

zh: 我们现在来到了最后的岔路口。我们追踪了哲学在两千五百年间的所有沧桑变迁。我们见证了它的辉煌与失败。我们曾有机会惊叹于人类智慧的巨大成就，并钦佩其视野的惊人广度与大胆。我们曾与历史上一些最伟大的思想家为伍。但如今，哲学史已走完其历程，而走完之后，又重新回到了起点。
en: We now arrive at a final parting of the ways. We have followed all the vicissitudes of philosophy over two-and-a-half millennia. We have participated in its triumphs and its failures.
