We have had occasion to marvel at the colossal achievements of the human intellect and admire the astonishing sweep and boldness of its vision. We have been in the presence of some of the greatest thinkers who have ever lived. But now the history of philosophy has run its course, and having done so, returns once again to its starting point.

zh: 正如我们所见，哲学始于古希腊。早期的爱奥尼亚哲学家是唯物主义者，他们认为物质对象具有生命，或者更确切地说，物质被赋予了一种与生俱来的生命力或能量。这正是“物活论”的确切含义。当泰勒斯说“万物皆充满神灵（daimon）”时，他指的就是这一点。所有早期希腊哲学家都主张，所有物质对象中都存在某种生命形式。他们认为磁铁因其吸引力而具有生命。这显然表明物质具有固有的运动能力。这一惊人的洞见比现代科学的发现早了两千五百年。
en: Philosophy, as we have seen, commences with the Greeks. The early Ionian philosophers were materialists who believed that material objects possessed life, or rather that matter is invested with a kind of innate life force, or energy. That is the exact meaning of hylozoism. It is what Thales meant when he said that all things are full of gods (daimon). All the early Greek philosophers taught that there is a form of life in all material objects. They regarded the magnet as alive because of its attractive powers. This apparently showed that matter possessed the inherent power of movement. This astonishing insight anticipated the discoveries of modern science by two-and-a-half millennia.

zh: 看起来，我们似乎已经完成了一个巨大的循环，如今又回到了出发点。但思想和科学的演进并非一个无尽的循环，而更像是一条螺旋——其中一种理论否定另一种理论，同时保留了早期阶段中所有可行且具有进步意义的内容。以旧有意义而言，哲学已经说尽了它所能说的一切有价值的内容。它已经完成了自己的使命，在此过程中，也耗尽了它曾经所拥有的一切进步潜力。今天的哲学，不过是昔日辉煌的可怜影子罢了。
en: It would seem that we have completed a great circle and have now returned to our point of departure. But the evolution of thought and science is not an endless circle, but rather a spiral, in which one theory negates another, while retaining all that was viable and progressive in the earlier stages. Philosophy in the old sense of the word has said everything worthwhile that it had to say. It has served its purpose, and in so doing, it has exhausted all the progressive potential that it once possessed. Philosophy today is only a pitiful shadow of its former self.

zh: 这绝非偶然。科学通过实验和观察这些可靠的手段，取代了空洞的推测和神秘主义这些无益的消遣，从而在很大程度上解开了人类曾经苦思冥想的重大谜团。古希腊前苏格拉底哲学家的唯物主义是一种卓越的预见，但实际上更像是一种灵感迸发的猜测。他们缺乏支持其主张的必要科学证明，因为当时的生产力尚未达到提供此类证明所需的水平。我们无需再回溯泰勒斯、阿那克西曼德和赫拉克利特的奇思妙想，因为我们掌握着科学在数十年乃至数个世纪的进程中所积累的丰富信息。
en: This is no accident. The great mysteries over which it used to ponder have been largely solved by the discoveries of science, which prefers the trusty weapons of experiment and observation to the useless pastimes of empty speculation and mystification. The materialism of the Greek pre-Socratic philosophers was a brilliant anticipation, but it was really in the nature of an inspired guess. They lacked the necessary scientific proof for their assertions, because the productive forces had not yet reached the level required to furnish such proofs. We do not have to return to the fantastic theories of Thales, Anaximander and Heraclitus, because we have at our disposal all the wealth of information provided by the march of science over many decades and centuries.

zh: 新的起点
en: A NEW DEPARTURE

zh: 正是在这一点上，我们抵达了一个全新的出发点，与以往所有哲学发生了根本性的分道扬镳。这一点在马克思《关于费尔巴哈的提纲》中或许最为宏大且重要的论述中得到了体现：那著名的第十一条提纲。这些话语如同号角般穿越时代回响，犹如一股清新的空气。哲学终于从那个被经院式思辨囚禁了几个世纪、阴暗而窒息的地窖中走出来，眯着眼被拖到了阳光之下。
en: Precisely at this point we have arrived at an entirely new point of departure, a fundamental parting of the ways with all previous philosophy. It finds its expression in what is perhaps the greatest and most important of Marx’s Theses on Feuerbach: the celebrated eleventh thesis. These words, which have echoed like a clarion call down the ages, are like a breath of fresh air. At long last, philosophy finally emerges out of the dark and airless cellar to which it was confined for centuries by scholastic speculation and is dragged, blinking, into the light of day.

zh: 在此，哲学思想——人类精神最高、最崇高的成就——首次不再仅仅是一种沉思活动，而是成为改变社会斗争中的一件利器。我们如今已离开哲学家那昏暗的书房，步入人类生活、活动与斗争的灿烂阳光之下。哲学终于不再是少数特权思想家的专利。它在实践中实现了它潜在的全部可能。
en: Here philosophical thought – the highest, most sublime achievement of the human spirit – for the first time ceases to be merely a contemplative activity and becomes a formidable weapon in the struggle to change society. We have now left the dimly lit study of the philosopher, and stepped out into the broad daylight of human life, activity and struggle. Finally, philosophy ceases to be a monopoly of a privileged handful of thinkers. It becomes in practice what it always was in potential.

zh: 马克思指出，思想本身既没有历史，也没有现实存在。它们既不打仗，也不赢得胜利。历史上的真正战斗是由男男女女进行的。在大多数情况下，推动他们行动的首要因素，并非仅仅是思想，而是物质条件。群众那种本能的、原始的革命运动，是社会主义革命的动力源泉。但整个历史都表明，自发行动是有限的。
en: Marx pointed out that ideas in themselves have no history and no real existence. They fight no battles and win no victories. The real battles of history are fought by men and women. And in most circumstances, they are moved in the first instance, not by ideas alone, but by material circumstances. The instinctive, elemental revolutionary movement of the masses is the mainspring of the socialist revolution. But all history shows the limitation of spontaneous action.

zh: 为了取得成功，无产阶级必须武装自己，掌握必要的思想、方法和纲领。马克思曾阐明，当思想深入群众心中时，便会成为一种物质力量。正是在这里，科学思想不再是无谓的消遣，而是与人类携手并进——不是“自我意识”或“世界精神”这类毫无生气的抽象概念，也不是费尔巴哈的抽象人类学构想，而是真实、鲜活、充满生命力、在斗争中奋战的男女。而我们——新世界观的战斗捍卫者——在汲取过去各种哲学中一切进步、真实和持久的内容的同时，也自豪地在我们的旗帜上高举马克思的箴言：
en: In order to succeed, the working class must be armed with the necessary ideas, methods and programme. And Marx explained that ideas become a material force when they grip the minds of the masses. Here is where scientific thought ceases to be an idle occupation and joins hands with humanity – not the lifeless abstractions of “Self-Consciousness” or “World Spirits” or Feuerbach’s abstract anthropological construction, but real, breathing, living, struggling, fighting men and women. And we, the militant defenders of the new world outlook, while embracing all that was progressive, truthful and enduring in the philosophies of the past, proudly proclaim on our banner the words of Marx:

zh: “哲学家们只是用各种不同的方式解释世界；问题的关键在于改变它。”
en: The philosophers have only interpreted the world in various ways; the point is to change it.
